#2819. NFL predictions: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Dolphins

The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) will face off in Week 9 in a battle between two teams at different stages in their regime builds. The Lions have their eyes firmly set on the postseason and are riding a three-game win streak, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild and are performing much like the Lions did in 2021 and 2022—lots of grit, but struggling to find success.

"(Dolphins Head) Coach (Jeff) Hafley's done a good job in his first year," Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday. "A lot of similarities to—just reminds me a little of what we were when we came in. They're young, they're hungry, they're active. They run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball, and they're playing that way."

This week's prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook, who currently have the Lions listed at +1600 to win this year's Super Bowl and are currently 7-point favorites in Week 9. Let's take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will earn a victory over the Dolphins in this week's Honolulu Blueprint.

For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 9 preview: Breaking down the Dolphins' offensive and defensive schemes.

Last Sunday, the Lions faced arguably the best defense in the NFL when they went head-to-head with the Vikings, and while the Dolphins are on the opposite end of the rankings spectrum, some of the strategies the Lions used against Minnesota will transfer over to this week's game against Miami.

The Dolphins defense enters this game 29th in DVOA, 24th in points allowed (25.9), 24th in yards allowed per play (5.7 ypp), and are dead last in the NFL in three areas: EPA per play (+0.10), EPA per pass allowed (+0.26), and passing yards allowed per play (8.3).

However, this defense is showing growth in pressure rate. Looking at season totals, the Dolphins' pressure numbers could be a bit deceiving: 31st in total pressures (77), 18th in pressure rate (35.6%), 30th in total sacks (9), and 28th in sack rate (4.2%). But when you look at the splits from their last four games, you can see the improvement:

at Vikings: 17 pressures, 39.5% pressure rate, 4 sacks, 9.3% sack rate

vs. Bengals: 11 pressures, 33.3% pressure rate, 0 sacks, 0% sack rate

at Jets: 15 pressures, 45.5% pressure rate, 2 sacks, 6.1% sack rate

vs. Patriots: 13 pressures, 48.1% pressure rate, 3 sacks, 11.1% sack rate

If we isolate the games against the Vikings, Jets, and Patriots, we see nearly 60% of the defensive pressures and 100% of the Dolphins sacks. When you look at how the Dolphins have generated pressures and sacks, most of those situations come from stunting their defensive linemen. Last week against the Patriots, the Dolphins sacked the quarterback once on an end-of-half situation, with the other two sacks coming off a stunt where an edge rusher loops behind the interior defensive lineman and twists inside. We also saw stunts get home against the Vikings in Week 4.

To counter the Dolphins' stunts, offenses have been attacking the middle of the defensive line with their rushing attacks; teams are running inside 53% of the time, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL.

While the Lions have preferred to lean on their outside-zone rushing scheme, we saw last week against the Vikings that Detroit has a formula to get downhill on inside runs. Now, the Lions don't necessarily need to deploy a full-house set (three players in the backfield) again, but it would certainly be effective against the Dolphins' Wide-9 base 4-3 defense.

While all defenses are complex, at their core, the Dolphins split their defensive personnel almost evenly between a base 4-3 (three linebackers) front and a "Big Nickel" (three safeties) formation. Regardless of set, they spend about 80% of the time in zone coverage, with half of that time spent between single-high (Cover-1, -3) and two-high (Cover-2, -4, -6) safety sets. When they deploy man coverage, they run exclusively single-high Cover-1.

Depending on the safety formation, Lions quarterback Jared Goff will have to find the holes in the zone to exploit, but those gaps can widen if the Lions stretch the Dolphins laterally with their passing game. Based on the games I watched, the Dolphins' defenders settle in their zones and tend to be slow to react to crossing routes in front of them. When offenses find success on crossers and stretch the zones across the field, that opens gaps down the deep seams, where speed receivers—hey, Jameson Williams—have found chunk plays.

If the Lions can slow the Dolphins' pass rush with run up the middle, then stretch the secondary laterally, they'll have an opportunity to chew up yards in a variety of ways.

When the Dolphins lost their dynamic running back De'Von Achane to an ACL injury in Week 3, many thought Miami's rushing attack would struggle. However, second-year back Ollie Gordon has stepped into a starting role, and the Dolphins' new downhill, physical rushing attack has proved to be an asset, even outproducing their early-season statistics, save last week vs. the Patriots. With quarterback Malik Willis adding another element to the run game through RPOs and scrambles, stopping the run will likely be the Lions' top priority.

On paper, their raw numbers look good: rushing for 123.3 yards per game (11th), averaging 4.4 yards per carry (11th), -0.03 EPA per rush (10th), 26 runs that gain 10+ yards (7th), and explosive runs 16.7% (3rd).

However, there are some concerning numbers that point to struggles with consistency, including:

The Dolphins will want to establish their rushing attack against the Lions, and Detroit will need to match that downhill physicality. It wouldn't be surprising to see the Lions spend a lot of time in base early as both teams work to control the trenches. Expect seven and eight defenders in the box pre-snap, and a situational spy to track Willis is likely.

With changes coming to the Lions' linebacker roles, Detroit will need Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske, and Malcolm Rodriguez to elevate their games and keep the explosive runs in check.

If the Dolphins can establish the run, they do a nice job of running play-action behind it and finding success. But that's not always an option for Miami's offense, and the inconsistencies in the run game have forced Willis to create opportunities on his own.

Willis is talented—we saw that in Green Bay—comfortable passing from the pocket, and able to extend plays by escaping outside. But with limited support, he holds onto the ball too long, takes sacks, or misses his targets because his accuracy gets loose/inconsistent on the run. Miami's offensive line is average at best (see below) and doesn't hold up well against pressure, and while the Dolphins receivers have unique skills, they lack a true playmaker and currently rely on two rookies—Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell—in starting wide receiver roles.

As a result, Miami's passing offense numbers are near the bottom of the league:

The Lions would benefit by giving Willis no relief. Entering this game, the Lions have registered 116 pressures (5th best), a 35.8% pressure rate (17th), 24 sacks (third most), and a 7.4% sack rate (7th). Defense has found success against the Dolphins by rushing four and sending the blitz, so the Lions should have options to create pressure; they just need to find the right elixir to disrupt Willis.

Like last season, the Dallas Cowboys are one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL in 2026.

After hearing from Brian Schottenheimer, Christian Parker, Klayton Adams, and most of the key players this week, it seems like there is a lot of reflecting going on inside The Star currently. With the decimated Indianapolis Colts coming up this week in the noon window, the Cowboys are desperate for a win, not only for their playoff hopes, but for the locker room sanity.

The Cowboys locker room is clearly frustrated with what's going on. While the talking point this week has been "execution", the Cowboys coaching staff needs to hold up their end of the bargain as well on the offensive side of the football.

Over the last three weeks, the Cowboys have converted 38.5%, 61.4% and 37.5% on third-down plays. The ups and downs of their season are attributed to execution.

"It's hard to say we're pressing," quarterback Dak Prescott said. "But, yeah, when you've got the talent we've got, when you've got the expectation, the standards that we have for ourselves and you go three-and-out or you don't score a touchdown, yeah, that's frustrating and you've got to make sure that you don't allow that to continue to bleed because then that bleeds into guys making [mistakes] or not doing the details the right way because they want the big play rather than just sticking to it."

The Cowboys lack of identify on offense points directly to their head coach and play-caller. Each week they seem to bounce back and forth from a run-first team to a pass-heavy team. That lack of consistency may be a big reason the team has been so inconsistent so far this season.

#2814. INTERVIEW: Club CEO Cramer feels Dortmund's "closeness" to its fans outshines silverware drought

MÜNCHEN (Bulinews): Despite having only laid claim to a pair of DFB-Pokal cups in the last decade, Borussia Dortmund's CEO Carsten Cramer feels the club offers “closeness” like none other as its main selling point.

“It’s a challenge, but I think in times like this, people are not looking for a club like Dortmund but they honour the way we act as a club," Cramer told Bulinews.com and others at a media round regarding grown their fan base.

“When we go to the US or Japan [in pre-season] we always try and open the doors to the club. We want to make fans feel they are part of our club which is something that is slightly different to the others.

“They [other big clubs] are slightly more business driven or entertainment driven. We try make good stuff on the digital channels to invite them [international supporters] to be part of our club.

“If they are only interested in trophies or the player in black and yellow with the Ballon d’Or, maybe that’s something we can’t offer to them. But we are able to offer a different approach and closeness – that’s the Dortmund way.

“I think even hardcore supporters of one club do have a sympathy for us as a second club [to support], which we don’t complain about. We are not too small to be a niche club, but we are a for sure a bit different," he added.

When asked as to how the Westphalian outfit can improve their relationship with fans abroad, Cramer pointed to the supporters themselves. He feels their reviews often help BVB shape their approach around the globe.

“They open our eyes to the needs and demands which is very useful [to the club]. I also love to travel around the world because the feedback I receive about the club is always extremely positive.

“People love how we honour our fans and supporters. They always give positive feedback that the efforts we make are worth it for them. We also have to expand our international market to generate growth.

“In Germany, everyone knows this. The [financial] cake is divided evenly, so we know there won’t be a bigger piece for us. That way the potential for growth is given to the international work we have to do," the BVB chief concluded.

#2813. Talking points as Premiership prepares for international break

The Scottish Premiership resumes for one more round of fixtures before this month's international break.

Six games, five kick-off times, lots of issues to address.

Last weekend turned out to be a good one for Rangers in more ways than one.

A late Ryan Naderi goal sealed a Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen on Saturday evening.

And, on Sunday at lunchtime, Premiership leaders Celtic lost in Falkirk, opening up the possibility of Rangers reducing the gap at the top to a point before the reigning champions host Kilmarnock on Sunday.

However, to do that, Derek McInnes' side, now unbeaten in 11 outings, must win away to St Mirren on Saturday.

The last time Rangers were in the Saturday 20:00 slot, they dropped two points away to Dundee and another warning for the Ibrox side is St Mirren's recent home form - a draw with Hibernian and a victory over in-form Dundee.

Craig McLeish's side havw won just once in eight games but ran Rangers pretty close the last time the sides met in Glasgow, only a late Bojan Miovski goal separating the sides.

The Buddies are holding their own in the Premiership this term, sitting eighth within touching distance of the top six at this early stage and St Mirren led Celtic in a Saturday night contest before eventually losing 2-1 in early September.

An intriguing match under the lights awaits.

Hibs were the other League Cup semi-final victors, coming from a goal down to beat Edinburgh rivals Heart of Midlothian 2-1 to end a seven-game run without a win.

The task for Marink Reedijk and his side now is to get their Premiership form in order before returning to Hampden to face Rangers in mid-December.

Under their new Duthc coach, Hibs have taken only one point from a possible 12 so far and prop up the table having played 11 games.

Aberdeen host the Edinburgh side on Saturday evening and the Dons themselves need a turnaround in fortunes in the league, having lost two in a row in the division prior to their semi-final defeat by Rangers.

Stephen Robinson's side are third from bottom, three points better off than Hibs, and the sides drew 1-1 at Easter Road only last month.

It's perhaps still a tad early to be talking in terms of crisis for either club, particularly given Hibs could end the calendar year with a trophy in the cabinet, but both teams need to get a bit of a move on to preserve their top-six ambitions.

Duran & Osmand spark Celtic into life - but where does that leave Hogh?

Late Duran double downs Besiktas to give Celtic first Europa League win

Injury-hit and error-ridden Hearts slump to defeat in Thun

Last week's Saturday results in the Premiership did little to break up the clutch of clubs jostling for position in the middle of the table.

It could be a similar story this weekend with Dundee United hosting Motherwell and a Tayside derby between St Johnstone and Dundee, with both at 15:00 GMT on Saturday.

Well ended their long wait for a win by beating St Mirren at home last weekend while St Johnstone twice fought back with 10 players to draw 2-2 with Kilmarnock as the Dundee duo had the weekend off.

Motherwell's 3-0 win over United in early September is their biggest of the league season so far, the visitors having played most of that match with 10 men.

The same day, Dundee thought they were on their way to three points when they led late on against Saints at Dens, but the Perth side had other ideas with an even later equaliser.

With Dundee one point behind Falkirk and United one point further back, both have the chance to move above the Bairns before they face Hearts on Sunday.

Celtic bounced back from defeat by Falkirk with a stirring 3-2 victory at home to Besiktas in the Europa League.

Earlier on Thursday, injury ravaged Hearts lost 3-1 to Thun in Switzerland.

As such, both Scottish sides play their Premiership fixtures on Sunday.

Rangers' result the night before will either offer encouragement or added pressure, with leaders Celtic four points clear of Rangers and the same margin of points between second place and Hearts as things stand.

With one win now in seven games and with 10 first-team players missing on Thursday, Wouter Vrancken and his squad are desperate for the respite provided by the international break.

First, though, the must host in-form Falkirk, who are bidding for five wins in a row. The Bairns' first league win of the campaign was at home to Hearts back in mid-September. They have seldom looked back.

By half-time at Tynecastle, Celtic will be getting ready to kick off against Kilmarnock. Misfiring Kasper Hogh's only three Celtic goals so far came in a 5-1 win at Rugby Park back in August.

Fellow summer signing Camilo Duran has done most of the scoring for Celtic since, including a double (a Duran Duran if you will) against Besiktas.

Whoever starts in attack for the hosts, second-bottom Killie will have their work cut out to improve a run of one win in six outings.

San Diego looks to advance to the NL Division Series when it takes on Chicago at 10 p.m. ET in Game 2 of their Wild Card showdown at Petco Park. After stranding the tying run at second base in the ninth inning of a 3-1 loss in the decisive third game at Wrigley Field last postseason, the Padres posted a dominant 8-0 victory in Tuesday's opener and can make their third trip to the NLDS in five years with a win on Wednesday.

Michael King held the Cubs to one hit over seven innings and Fernando Tatis Jr. set the tone by homering on the first pitch of the game by Chicago's Matthew Boyd as San Diego banged out 13 hits. Manny Machado also went deep in the first inning, and Xander Bogaerts added a solo shot in the fourth for the Padres, who have gone 18-3 since Sept. 6.

The Padres attempt to end this matchup behind right-hander Nick Pivetta, who will be making just his fifth start since returning from a nearly five-month absence due to an elbow injury. The 33-year-old has allowed a total of three runs over 18 2/3 innings in his four outings since rejoining the rotation.

The Cubs turn to Kevin Gausman as they hope to force a Game 3. The 35-year-old righty, who was acquired from the Toronto Blue Jays at the trade deadline in early August, has yielded fewer than three runs in three of his last four starts but came away with just one victory during that stretch.

Boston looks to register more than three hits when it faces left-hander Max Fried, who limited the Red Sox to one run and six hits over 11 2/3 frames in two starts this year. #2810. Lakers assign Bronny Games to G League Coachella Valley Lakers

What do the Lakers need as other guards around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves? Shooters, ideally ones who can defend as well.

That is leaving Bronny James squeezed. The Lakers have assigned Bronny to the Coachella Valley Lakers of the G League, along with first-round pick Cameron Carr. This is mostly about getting the two young Lakers run they aren't getting with the big club, which is off to a 7-2 start.

Bronny has played 12 minutes across five games so far this season, largely in mop-up duty at the end of games. His being sent to the G League isn't new, in each of his first two NBA seasons, he bounced between the G League and the big club.

The issue is the Lakers need guards who are shooters and Bronny is not that, even if he hit 38.6% from 3 last season (he is 0-for-1 from deep this season). To his credit, Bronny has really developed through his first two NBA seasons. He has a good feel for the game, he can defend well (but at 6'2" doesn't really guard up), he can get into the paint some and make good reads, but he's not the guy the Lakers need right now.

Carr, the Lakers' first-round pick out of Baylor, is incredibly athletic but is raw, which is why he has played in a total of four minutes across three games. He needs to be down in the G League just to get some run.

The Lakers G League team opens play Friday at the Acrisure Arena just outside Palm Springs. The Lakers moved their G League franchise there this summer from El Segundo (they used to practice at the Lakers facility).

#2805. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2804. Lakers vs. Blazers Preview: It’s payback time

The Lakers (7-2) are back home, where they will host a rematch with the Portland Trail Blazers (6-1) on Friday. The matchup will also serve as an NBA Cup contest, with both teams competing in West Group C.

Who: Los Angeles Lakers vs. Portland Trail Blazers

One of the Lakers' two losses this season came at the hands of the Trail Blazers, who ran the purple and gold off their home floor last week. That was the same game that exposed the Lakers' early flaws such as their inability to rebound the ball well, over reliance on Luka Dončić and overall team defense. While those weaknesses are still apparent, the Lakers have done a better job of navigating them and responding since that loss.

On Friday, they have the chance to get even.

This will be a good opportunity to see whether the Lakers have learned from their loss, how they've adjusted and how determined they are to make a run in the NBA Cup after losing pretty badly in the opener against the Warriors.

Here are three storylines worth noting ahead of the matchup between the Lakers and Blazers:

Morant was a huge factor in the Blazers' first victory over the Lakers, posting 23 points. He easily got in the paint and scored nine out of his 13 attempts. It felt like the Lakers had no answer for him. Fortunately for the purple and gold, they won't have to think about Ja on Friday because he's currently recovering from a Grade 2 hamstring injury.

Instead, the Lakers should expect more touches for Deni Avdija, Damian Lillard and Scoot Henderson, who replaced Morant in the starting lineup.

Defense will be the biggest key for the Lakers if they want to come away with a win. In their previous meeting, Los Angeles allowed Portland to shoot 50% from beyond the arc while giving up 56 points in the paint. The Blazers' hot shooting may have been an outlier but there's no guarantee it won't happen again if the Lakers don't tighten things up defensively. The Blazers have enough scoring to match the Lakers' firepower.

Portland is the seventh-best rebounding team in the league and currently has a top-10 offensive and defensive rating. They lead the league in points per game (121.9), which is why they're a tough cover. This isn't one of those teams the Lakers can just overwhelm with Dončić's brilliance and talent alone. They'll have to work on both ends of the floor.

If their first NBA Cup match was any indication, the Lakers didn't seem too interested in making a statement, which is unfortunate because these games are so much fun to win. Hopefully that changes for this one because it's pretty much a do-or-die game for the Lakers if they want to stay alive in the NBA Cup. Not only are they 0-1, they have a concerning -17 point differential and, if they want to increase their chances of advancing, they're going to need to win in some blow outs.

It's a tough task but one the purple and gold should aim to do if they truly want to exact revenge against the Blazers on Friday.

The Lakers and Warriors are the only ones in West Group C that have played in the NBA Cup so far, but expect the standings to change on Friday when the Spurs and Kings go at it.

For the Lakers' injury report, Sandro Mamukelashvili (illness) is listed as questionable.

#2803. Illinois volleyball falls short in unranked matchup to UCLA

CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Illinois needs some momentum heading to the homestretch of the season.

It didn't get it on Thursday night at Huff Hall as UCLA dispatched the Illini in four sets.

Head coach Chris Tamas made a bold lineup change, entrusting sophomore Sophi Randall to the starting setter position. This comes after Randall has been splitting sets with senior Kenna Phelan, whose spark seems to have dimmed. Randall has looked strong in recent matchups, with an exciting slide connection with middle Ashlyn Philpot.

UCLA was a great matchup for the Illini at this point in the season, as both teams are strong and unranked. To add on, UCLA entered the night on a four-match losing streak. This wasn't necessarily a "must win," but the momentum would've been nice looking ahead to a tough schedule.

Illinois threw the first punch of the night, winning the first set 25-17. However, it only went down from there. The Illini block coverage diminished in the second set, and the front row went silent. A glimmer of hope for the Illini Thursday was no doubt sophomore outside Alyssa Aguayo.

After a rough second and third set — Illinois dropped both, 25-15, 25-21 — Aguayo stood out in a struggling Illini lineup. Aguayo led the team with a whopping 19 kills, setting her career high. A strength of Aguayo's is her ability to slow the game down, and play technically. She is a player that is beautiful to watch, and holds herself in a composed manner. Head coach Chris Tamas agrees too.

"She's very steady and someone we rely on a lot," Tamas said. "We're gonna continue to rely on her as the season goes on."

The fourth set was a change in momentum for the Illini, senior Kenna Phelan entered the game in hopes to bring some defensive stability to the team. The change was definitely much needed, and lit a fire underneath her squad. The set was back-and-forth, with the Illini pushing the Bruins to a tie at 24-24. A serving error by Paityn Chapman returned UCLA the rock, and the game was ended by a blocked dump-set from Phelan.

That same story got told a lot Thursday night as the Illini managed to rack up 13 serving errors, led by freshman phenom Maya Harris with 4, and closely followed by Randall, who chipped in 3. The serving errors mixed with 23 attack errors, led to a flat outing.

The Illini now travel to face No. 22 Indiana, and undefeated No. 1 Nebraska, then meet No. 11 Penn State at Huff Hall. After this gauntlet of games, the Illini only have one opportunity to catch a breath of fresh air (unranked Iowa on Nov. 17) before heading to the first Big Ten Volleyball Tournament.

#2801. INTERVIEW: Roy Makaay on the success of FC Bayern's World Squad and unearthing talents like Maycon Cardozo

MÜNCHEN (Bulinews) Well into it's sixth year in operation, Roy Makaay can't speak any higher of Bayern Munich's World Squad. Speaking at a round table event where Bulinews.com was present, he detailed some of the initiative's successes.

“Six years ago, Bayern gave players under 19 [years old] a chance to be part of the Bayern Munich family. The first three years Klaus Augenthaler was the coach and then they asked me,” the 51-year-old former Bayern star explained.

“My coaching experience [helps], we speak English and Spanish because we don’t speak German in this World Squad with the staff. In the beginning people thought it was just a social project because the kids have to apply by sending a video.

“Of course, a lot of them have agents, but they have to upload a video and then we select them through the video [based on their skills]. They [the submissions] are getting better and better every year [since I started] coaching.

“The first two weeks we went abroad. We went to Argentina and then the last two weeks we are always at the Sabener Strasse. Then on the last day we always play a match against Bayern’s under-19 academy team.

“In the last four years we have beaten them twice, and they [Bayern] don’t like it that the academy team loses to a team that doesn’t know each other. We now have 20 to 25 players who have turned pro from the World Squad," he smiled.

The 46-time Netherlands international focused in on two names in particular - his stories of World Squad defender Ignacio Isla and Bayern talent Maycon Cardozo's rise to becoming professional footballers are particularly striking.

“A couple of days ago I got a message from Argentinean centre-back Ignacio Isla. He was at Unión Santa Fe and made his professional debut this week, so we can add another [successful player] to the list [of graduates].

“I think the biggest [World Squad star] is Maycon Cardozo. He joined us aged 15 years old. […] He played at [Bayern’s] Thailand academy and showed his quality, so we decided to keep him for one more week with Bayern’s under-17 team.

“He turned 16 that January, so he signed for them but got injured straight away with his shoulder. Last year he was playing with the under-19 side and one day I was speaking with Kompany.

“He said that one of your players [Cardozo] is training with our panel. He said the little Brazilian-Portuguese guy. All of a sudden, he was playing with Kompany’s team as he gives a lot of time for young players to train with the first team.

“He got his debut against Gladbach. It was 3-0 [to Bayern] with a red card. The camera turned to the side and he was coming on [as a sub]. I was proud, but prouder for the people who invented [the World Squad] six years ago.

“I am only the coach but there’s a lot of hard work behind the scenes in the offices. [Things like] arranging the visas, because it’s not that easy to get to some countries anymore,” Makaay said, making sure to praise the staff's communal effort.

#2797. Game Recap: Booker drops 30 as Suns secure win over Magic, 117-104

It was a much-needed victory for the Suns tonight as they improved to 2-5 on the season.

Phoenix spotted Orlando an early lead, then took the game over with its defense and its shooting. The Suns beat a short-handed Magic team without Paolo Banchero, Jalen Suggs and Jonathan Isaac, 117-104, to improve to 2-5. Phoenix was short Mark Williams, Jordan Goodwin, and Rasheer Fleming.

Orlando outrebounded Phoenix by 15 and got to the line 11 more times, but the Magic turned it over 25 times, and the Suns hit 17 threes. A 23-point lead after three quarters was more than enough to survive a late Orlando push.

Devin Booker: 30 points (11-of-22 FG, 4-of-8 3PT, 4-of-4 FT), 8 assists, 3 steals, +16 in 34 minutes

Dillon Brooks: 24 points (9-of-16 FG, 4-of-6 3PT), 2 steals, +12 in 29 minutes

Miles Bridges: 18 points (6-of-10 FG, 3-of-6 3PT), 13 rebounds, 5 assists, +12 in 31 minutes

Orlando came out firing. The Magic got whatever they wanted early and jumped out to a 14-8 lead.

Then the Suns started taking the ball away. Orlando turned it over nine times in the quarter, and Phoenix turned those mistakes into 13 points, mostly in transition. Anthony Black had four of those giveaways by himself.

Devin Booker played all 12 minutes and set the tone with 12 points, hitting a pair of threes and going perfect at the line. The Suns hit five threes as a team to Orlando's three, which covered for getting outworked on the glass and in the paint.

The bench changed the game. Ryan Dunn, Collin Gillespie and Man Man all finished the quarter on the plus side, and Phoenix pushed the lead to nine before Orlando got the last bucket to cut it to seven entering Q2.

Phoenix led after the first quarter, 33-26.

Luke Kennard owned the second quarter. He came off the bench and went 3-for-3 from deep for 12 points, giving Phoenix a second scorer while Orlando keyed in on Booker.

Booker kept cooking anyway. He added 11 more in the quarter on efficient shooting and went into the locker room with 23.

Orlando stayed close by crashing the glass and living at the line. The Magic grabbed nine offensive rebounds in the quarter and got to the stripe 14 times, but they missed six of those free throws and couldn't buy a three. Wendell Carter Jr. did most of the damage inside with 10 in the quarter.

Man Man didn't score, but he was a team-best +13 in his minutes.

The three-point line is the story. Phoenix hit 10 threes in the half and Orlando hit four. The Magic shot better inside and controlled the boards, but the Suns' shooting and Orlando's turnovers built the cushion.

Booker leads all scorers with 23 points on 8-of-13 shooting, including 3-of-4 from three and 4-of-4 at the line. Kennard has 12 off the bench.

Dillon Brooks took over the third. He scored 12 in the quarter on 5-of-7 shooting, and Miles Bridges added 10 more as the starters blew the game open.

Orlando's turnover problem came back in a big way. The Magic gave it away 10 times in the quarter, and Phoenix's defense jumped passing lanes all period with six steals.

Booker only scored three in the quarter, but he didn't need to. He set up teammates with four assists, and every Suns starter finished the period at +7 or better. Man Man chipped in a pair of buckets off the bench.

After three, Phoenix led 96-73. The Suns outscored Orlando 33-22 in the third quarter.

Orlando kept its starters on the floor and made a push, winning the quarter by 10. Carter didn't miss in the fourth, going 4-for-4, and the Magic knocked down five threes in the period.

Phoenix rested Booker and most of the starting group for long stretches, and the offense cooled off with five turnovers and three missed free throws in the quarter.

The deep bench closed it out, with Koa Peat, Jamaree Bouyea, Duop Reath and Pat Spencer getting the final minutes. Phoenix won 117-104.

Kevin Durant returns to the Valley on Saturday night as the Suns host the Houston Rockets.

With 5 receptions against the 49ers on Sunday, Bowers would surpass Trey McBride for the most receptions for a tight end in their first three seasons.

If you're a tight end fan, this is the game to watch. Over the years, the position has evolved from a security blanket and last read for QBs to a role where tight ends can run like wide receivers and are heavily relied on in the passing and running game.

#2795. 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. the Atlanta Falcons

The 5-2 Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the 9:30 a.m. ET game this week in Madrid, Spain. Their opponent will be the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons.

While Atlanta doesn't have the greatest record in the league, they have been a tough out almost every week, with a big victory just 2 weeks ago against the San Francisco 49ers.

What are 3 keys to the Cincinnati Bengals leaving Spain with a victory this week? Let's dive into it.

You are never going to completely shut down Bijan Robinson. He is the best running back in football. He isn't just elite at running the ball, but he is dynamic at catching passes out of the backfield. He is about to eclipse 1,000 all-purpose yards on the season already, but hasn't run for over 80 rushing yards in the last 3 weeks of the season. I do not want to be the team that he goes off against after a few subpar performances by his standards.

It will be a total team effort if they are going to keep him in check this week. They cannot have missed tackles like they have been known for over the past few seasons. Robinson will make you pay if you let him slip out of your initial grasp. If the Bengals want to win this game, they have to find a way to not allow Robinson to go nuclear.

While the Bengals are never going to be a run-centric team, this is a week they have to find some balance. Atlanta lost to Tampa Bay last week, 16-0, in a rainy game that the Buccaneers did not complete a single pass in. They were able to instead rush for over 300 yards against the Falcons' defense.

They have done that without James Pearce Jr., who is returning from an 8-game suspension this week. This is not a game you want to be throwing the ball almost 50 times. Establish some balance with getting carries and short passes to Chase Brown and Samaje Perine this week.

If you don't, you will see Atlanta get the victory.

Michael Penix is completing 61% of his passes this season. He has just 9 passing touchdowns to 5 interceptions. If the Bengals can get pressure on Penix this week, you can force him into some turnovers. Boye Mafe is 6th in the league for defensive ends with 35 pressures this season.

The Bengals also have a dangerous interior pass rush with Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen on the interior. Both of those guys are in the top 12 for defensive tackles in pressures, with 24 for Dexter and 23 for Allen.

Myles Murphy is coming off his second game in the last 3 played where he recorded 5 pressures on the day. Without Cashius Howell this week, they will need a guy like Murphy to continue generating pressure opposite Boye Mafe.

#2793. Trevor Lawrence is having by far the best season of his career

Trevor Lawrence has so much talent for the quarterback position that if freshmen could declare for the NFL draft, Lawrence probably would have been the first overall pick in 2019, when he had just led Clemson to a national championship as a true freshman. Instead, Lawrence stayed three years at Clemson and was the first pick in 2021, viewed as a sure-thing quarterback prospect.

In Year 6, Lawrence finally looks like everything he was supposed to be.

Lawrence is having by far the best year of his NFL career, with career-high stats across the board that are constrained only by the fact that the Jaguars win so many blowouts that Lawrence doesn't throw many passes in the fourth quarter.

So far this season, Lawrence has completed 146 of 224 passes for 1,932 yards, with 18 touchdowns, four interceptions and an NFL-leading passer rating of 111.7. Project Lawrence's totals to a 17-game season, and he's on pace to finish with 4,106 yards, 38 touchdowns and nine interceptions. Those are MVP numbers.

Lawrence's rookie year was a disaster, as he led the league in interceptions while playing on a chaotic Jaguars team coached by Urban Meyer, whose only foray into NFL coaching lasted less than one season. Lawrence and the Jaguars got a lot better once they kicked Meyer to the curb, but even in the next three years with Doug Pederson, an offensive coach with a Super Bowl-winning pedigree, Lawrence didn't live up to the pre-draft hype.

Playing in Liam Coen's offense, something has changed. Last year the Jaguars went 13-4, winning double-digit games for the first time since drafting Lawrence, and this year Lawrence and the Jaguars are even better. Lawrence's average of 8.6 yards per pass is the best of his career by almost a yard and a half, a remarkable improvement for any quarterback to make in his sixth season.

Lawrence has thrown touchdown passes on 8 percent of his attempts, the best in the NFL this season and by far the best mark of his career. And after getting sacked a career-high 41 times last year, Lawrence has gotten much more comfortable reading the pass rush in his second year in Coen's offense and has only been sacked 13 times this season.

Lawrence's numbers would look even better if the Jaguars weren't so often taking their foot off the gas late in games because they're blowing opponents out. Lawrence has 1,196 yards and 12 touchdowns in the first halves of games this season, but he only has 736 yards and six touchdowns in the second halves of games.

The Jaguars currently have the fourth-best odds to win the Super Bowl, and Lawrence has the fifth-best odds to win MVP. That might be underselling them, and him. The Jaguars may just be the best team, with the best quarterback, in the NFL right now.

#2792. Preview: Utah Jazz head for a rodeo in Dallas

The sky is falling. The Utah Jazz remain winless thus far in November, on the cusp of a six-game losing streak. The team is shooting 27.6% on wide-open threes and has been trailing the bottom of nearly every statistical category. But just maybe, just maybe, all they need is a good ol' NBA Cup Tournament match to light a competitive spirit under them.

That's right, the Dallas Mavericks host the Utah Jazz at the American Airlines Center for an Emirates NBA Cup West Group A showdown. Dallas has already gained an early 1-0 advantage in the Cup standings in their 116-111 victory over the Rockets just last week. The NBA Cup has not been favorable towards the Jazz since its inauguration; in fact, it's given teams more of an excuse to continue brutally beating up tanking teams — point differential matters!

Over the past few years, the Jazz have held records of:

But now that they're playing for wins (or so we've been told), we could see the script flipped. After all, it's a 'blank slate' for this young team. They've battled through injuries, have been a part of two overtime games, and have been through some of the worst shooting woes in years. But that's only temporary, right?

Dallas has likely been content with the Cooper Flagg-Kyrie Irving pairing, given that their team is 4-4 and has lost to some of the league's best. The Mavs play an incredibly fast brand of basketball, ranking among the league leaders in overall pace and fast-break points.

Obviously, Utah won't be able to put the reigning Rookie of the Year to a complete stop, but this team has to make an effort to command their presence in the paint. The Jazz allowed an unanswered 12-0 run by New Orleans in overtime just 48 hours ago, exclusively inside the arc. We saw them hold Zion Williamson completely scoreless in the first half, but all hell broke loose after they surrendered a 13-point lead. We'll have to hope that they can put out the same energy as they did against a conference foe like Flagg.

You could consider Cooper Flagg as an honorary 'Jazz Killer'. In his two career matchups, he averages 34.0 points, 8.5 rebounds and 7.0 assists. Though, the Jazz have won both of those matches. Now, with a reinforced Mavs squad around him, Utah can't roll into Dallas with a smug grin.

The numbers don't lie; Flagg has struggled tremendously from deep early into the season, shooting 7-of-33 from outside this season. Utah will have to force Flagg into uncomfortable shots that take him away from the line, where he converts 55.9% of his two-point attempts.

Because of his promoted role as a secondary playmaker, they should also employ a player like Ace or Okogie to pressure him into his loose handle and perhaps cough up a few turnovers — Flagg is averaging 3.1 turnovers per game in the early going of the season.

As one of the rising superstars in the West, he's transcended a typical 'sophomore slump' to turn Dallas into a legitimate playoff team this year. Finding a way to slow down this multifaceted star will be a burden on this team for the foreseeable future.

This has been a popular piece circulating Jazz Twitter:

Through the first eight games, the furthest milestone Peterson has achieved is really only being thrust in the starting lineup. He's averaged an honest 30.3 minutes per game, but the question is, why hasn't it felt like it?

He shares the ball with a dominant guard like Keyonte George, who completely dictates the tempo of the offense. Peterson's role shifts to that of a more complementary piece — a player that the team can chuck the ball to throw up a Hail Mary before the shot clock expires. Coach Hardy runs an egalitarian, pass-and-cut offensive system where Peterson is used to distort the defense rather than being a centerpiece.

Of course, he has his rookie mistakes too: he's hitting just 35.4% of his field-goal attempts, struggling to find a consistent rhythm inside the arc, particularly on his floater attempts. That could look particularly concerning, considering that he was noted for his lack of vertical burst coming out of the draft.

But after looking at the Darius Acuff Jr. template over at Sacramento (not recommended if you want to win basketball games), the coaching staff needs to realize they have DARRYN PETERSON on their squad. This is to hope they could have more plays run for him: perhaps using him more as a post-up guard, or having him be the one to leak up the court in transition.

If the Jazz are going to be without Jackson Jr. for a couple of months at least, and if Lauri Markkanen is unable to break out of his shooting slump, Peterson will need to play an integral part of the offensive flow moving forward.

Speaking of Lauri, the most unprecedented story coming out of this 1-7 start has been the Finnish Star's efficiency. Of course, we all saw him injure his wrist in the showdown against the Grizzlies, which has had lingering issues due to the dependence on his wrist snap & flick, but this is going to be an integral year for Lauri.

The drop-off has been stark: he's averaging 17.1 points per game — down significantly since his career peak and is converting just 38.7% of his field-goal attempts. The Hardy revolution has completely eradicated Markkanen's inside-the-arc scoring, having him attempt a wild 8.3 three-point attempts a game.

He's also been forced to occasionally shift as a small-ball center due to the banged-up injuries of Jackson Jr. and Nurkic, which was noticeably felt when the Pelicans destroyed the Jazz in the paint during the OT period.

"I think he's playing through a lot of pain right now. I think he's really battling for his teammates and us", Will Hardy said about Lauri Markkanen on Wednesday.

Of course, Markkanen will not have as wild a slump as he does for the rest of the season. He'll regain his efficiency. His wrist will eventually heal. Really, it's just a tough spot to be in when your team's record is 1-7.

#2791. Red Wings Rookie Delivers Mature Message After Heartbreaking Loss to Vegas

The Detroit Red Wings suffered another heartbreaking defeat Thursday night, but one of their youngest players delivered a message that sounded like it came from a seasoned NHL veteran.

Anton Johansson, the 22-year-old rookie defenseman who scored Detroit's only goal against the Vegas Golden Knights, wasn't interested in pointing fingers after the Red Wings surrendered a late lead and eventually lost 2-1.

Instead, Johansson emphasized something that could be just as important as his development on the ice: accountability, teamwork, and sticking together when things go wrong.

Oct 31, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings defenseman Anton Johansson (42) skates with the puck in the first period against the St. Louis Blues at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Detroit appeared headed for at least one point against Vegas before Trevor Connelly scored with just 1:42 remaining in regulation. The goal handed the Golden Knights a 2-1 victory and left the Red Wings searching for answers.

But when Johansson was asked about the frustrating finish, he offered a remarkably composed response.

"There are mistakes all the time out there," Johansson said following Thursday's loss. "We just have to back each other up. We learn from it, and we bounce back against Colorado."

That's an impressive perspective from a player still experiencing his first NHL season.

Johansson didn't single out a teammate for the late defensive breakdown, nor did he attempt to excuse the result. He acknowledged that mistakes happen and emphasized the importance of responding together.

For a Red Wings team navigating a difficult start to the season, that's exactly the kind of attitude that can help strengthen a locker room.

Johansson did more than offer encouraging words Thursday night. He also provided Detroit's only offensive breakthrough in an otherwise frustrating game.

With the score tied 0-0 early in the third period, Carter Mazur fired a shot that bounced off the end boards and directly toward Johansson near the right face-off circle. The rookie quickly buried the opportunity, giving Detroit a 1-0 lead at the 2:02 mark.

It was Johansson's second goal of the season and another encouraging moment for a young defenseman still establishing himself in the NHL.

The Red Wings couldn't protect the advantage, however. Braeden Bowman tied the game just over two minutes later before Connelly delivered the winner in the closing minutes.

According to the NHL's official game recap, Daniil Tarasov stopped 32 shots, while Vegas goaltender Carter Hart made 25 saves.

Despite the disappointing result, Johansson believed Detroit had played well enough to deserve a better outcome.

"It's hard. I think we played a good game. I think the second half of the first period, I think, was ours. I think the second period was ours. I think we started the third a little bit sloppy, but we got into it. We got a goal. It's hard. Just got to bounce back."

What makes Johansson's response especially encouraging is how quickly he appears to be embracing the responsibilities of playing in Detroit.

Selected in the fourth round of the 2022 NHL Draft, Johansson entered training camp fighting for an opportunity to establish himself with the Red Wings.

As we previously reported when Detroit's rookies discussed the support they've received from veterans, Johansson credited the team's experienced players for helping him adjust to the NHL.

That support appears to be paying dividends.

Johansson has already demonstrated the ability to contribute offensively, including his memorable first NHL goal against Philadelphia.

Now he's showing that his development isn't limited to skating, defending, and finding the back of the net.

His willingness to accept the result without assigning blame suggests he's learning how to handle the emotional side of professional hockey as well.

Detroit dropped to 7-7-3 following Thursday's defeat and has now lost three of its past four games. The Red Wings will begin a four-game road trip Saturday against the Colorado Avalanche.

That makes Johansson's message particularly timely.

The Red Wings don't have much time to dwell on what went wrong against Vegas. They need to regroup quickly before facing another difficult opponent.

My take: Johansson's comments might be one of the most encouraging things to come out of Thursday's loss.

It's easy for a young player to celebrate after scoring a goal. It's much harder to maintain perspective when that goal isn't enough to help his team win.

He recognized the disappointment, refused to blame anyone, and turned his attention toward the next challenge.

The Red Wings didn't get the result they wanted Thursday night, but they received another encouraging glimpse of what Anton Johansson could become.

#2789. What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique

What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

They're a team of superstars that don't play superstar basketball.

That's the beauty of this 76ers team. They play a brand of unselfish team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars.

LeBron James is one of the two or three greatest players in NBA history, a four-time MVP, a four-time NBA champion, a 1st-ballot Hall of Famer.

Joel Embiid is a seven-time all-star, a former MVP, an Olympic gold medalist and a likely Hall of Famer.

Jaylen Brown is a five-time all-star, an NBA champion, a career 20 points-per-game scorer.

Tyrese Maxey is a two-time all-star, one of only two NBA guards averaging 27.0 points per game over the last four years.

Four certified megastars on one team. And somehow they've figured out how to leave their egos at the front door and play smart, tough, disciplined team basketball, the style of ball you just never see on these superstar-laden teams.

On offense, they patiently work the ball around, always looking for the open man or a positive matchup. You've got this bunch of big-name, high-priced All-Stars who are just as happy to pass the ball as shoot it. That never happens.

The 76ers are sixth in the NBA in assists, and they're one of only four teams with twice as many assists as turnovers. Smart, unselfish, patient, disciplined.

When an all-timer like LeBron averages 7.3 assists per game that speaks volumes. LeBron is fifth in the NBA in assists per game among forwards, which is wild. You can see the joy on his face when one of his passes leads to a basket. When one of the greatest players in history has that mentality, it rubs off on everyone around him.

Embiid hasn't really got going yet on offense and still takes too many 3's, but he's also embraced the team-first mentality, and his 4.8 assists per game are more than one full assist above his career average and 4th-most in the NBA among centers or forward-centers. And still one of the most dominating defensive players in the league.

Brown is averaging 27.0 points, which you expect, but he's also averaging 4.3 assists per game, significantly above his career average of 3.8 coming into the season. He's fit in so well so fast you forget its his first season here.

And what can you even say about Maxey? Just a beast. He's averaging nearly 30 points per game but never wastes a possession, always makes the right decision with the ball in his hands and is still finding time to average 4.3 assists per game.

With James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey, the 76ers are the only NBA team with four guys averaging at least 16 points and 4 assists per game. Only the Pacers, Magic and Raptors have three.

But where we're really seeing this group playing out of their minds is on the defensive end, where this bunch of all-stars, including two newcomers, has been astounding.

The 76ers have the 2nd-best defensive efficiency rating in the league, behind only the Pistons, who they play Wednesday night, and they're allowing the 2nd-fewest points in the league, also behind Detroit. Last year, they allowed 123 points per game through eight games. This year they're at 111.

They're holding teams to 43 percent shooting from the field, 3rd-best in the league and their lowest since 2011-12. Their 9.3 steals per game are 6th-most.

All five starters are among the top 25 players in the league in defensive rating – James is fourth, Embiid 11th, Edgecombe 15th, Maxey 22nd and Brown 23rd. How is that even possible?

It's rare to see superstar-caliber guys play as hard on the defensive end as the offensive end. Everybody on this team embraces it. They hustle, they work, they communicate and most importantly they commit to it.

The biggest concern when the 76ers built this dream team was that it would be a team of individuals out for themselves, but the reality has been the opposite.

In a very short period of time, they've learned how to play together. How to play for each other.

And we haven't even mentioned V.J. Edgecomb, who at 21 years old has figured out how to assimilate into this loaded lineup, never force anything, wait for his opportunities and make huge shots when he gets his turn. Edgecombe is at 12.7 points and 3.0 assists per game, and his numbers are understandably down a bit from last year, but if that bothers him it sure doesn't show.

And the role players – Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jabari Walker – have each adopted the same ego-free style of basketball, supporting the starters however they need to.

Nick Nurse deserves a ton of credit for getting this bunch to play this brand of hoops. It's not easy to get any NBA player to put team goals ahead of individual goals. But he's got Hall of Famers and all-stars doing it and having a blast along the way. They all seem to love playing basketball the right way and they seem to love playing together.

The 76ers are 7-1 and looking like a real threat to win the East, and they're doing it by playing the game the right way.

By committing to each other and not themselves.

#2787. 4 keys to a Jets win vs. the Chiefs in Week 9

The New York Jets don't have much room for error as they enter Week 9. At 2-6, another defeat would extend a frustrating stretch and make a return to relevance nearly impossible. The challenge is substantial. Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes have built a track record of making opponents pay for even the smallest mistakes.

The Kansas City Chiefs enter Week 9 at 5-2, but consecutive losses have shown some vulnerability. That doesn't mean they are suddenly an easy opponent, especially at Arrowhead Stadium. The Jets will need to play with discipline, maintain control of the game's tempo, and take advantage of their opportunities.

New York has shown flashes of being competitive, but turning those moments into a complete performance is another matter. These four things will be especially important to ensure a victory on Sunday.

The Jets won the time-of-possession battle against the Las Vegas Raiders, but barely. New York held the ball for 30:02 compared with 29:58 for the Raiders. Las Vegas also had three scoring drives that lasted at least five minutes, while the Jets had only two. That won't be good enough against Mahomes.

One of the best ways to challenge Reid's offense is to keep it on the sideline. Longer possessions would give Glenn's defense more time to recover while putting additional pressure on the Kansas City defense to stay on the field.

Dylan Laube's second-quarter kickoff return for a touchdown changed the complexion of Sunday's game. Without that breakdown, the Jets could have carried a much larger advantage into halftime.

There's no way to know how the rest of the game would have unfolded, but surrendering seven points without the defense having an opportunity to make a stop is difficult to overcome, maybe. One can never tell. Maybe

New York has allowed too many momentum-changing special teams plays. Against Mahomes on the road, giving away a touchdown is a luxury the Jets simply cannot afford.

The Jets cannot afford to abandon the running game if the offense doesn't find immediate success. That becomes particularly important against a Kansas City defense allowing just 96.3 rushing yards per game, with only seven other teams surrendering fewer entering Week 9.

Staying competitive on the scoreboard will allow New York to remain patient and maintain some balance. Falling behind by multiple scores would make that considerably harder, putting too much responsibility on Smith and the passing game.

Geno Smith and Braelon Allen need to carry their Week 8 production into this matchup. Allen is coming off a 147-yard performance, a big boost for an offense that finally showed some explosiveness.

However, moving the ball between the 20-yard lines won't be enough. The Jets enter Week 9 ranked last in the NFL in red-zone touchdown percentage at 42.3%, and they converted just two of six opportunities against Las Vegas. Field goals won't consistently keep pace with Kansas City. New York needs touchdowns.

Kansas City is built to punish opponents who let the game get away from them. The Jets need to make this a game of patience and execution rather than one dictated by Mahomes and the Chiefs' offensive firepower. New York has spent too many Sundays watching opportunities slip away. This time, it must make the most of every chance before the final minutes arrive.

#2785. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2783. Is Derrick Henry seeking trade amid Ravens' collapse?

Derrick Henry has defied Father Time throughout the latter stages of his NFL career, but at 32, he only has a finite amount of elite play left in him. It's largely going to waste for a Baltimore Ravens team that's in complete free fall right now.

With Lamar Jackson and Tyler "Snoop" Huntley on injured reserve, Baltimore doesn't have much reason for optimism after four straight losses, including three by 20+ points. Jacoby Brissett is certainly not the answer.

Henry is doing what he can, ranking top 10 in the NFL in rushing yards and touchdowns, but he can't do it all. Still, he's not looking at an exit plan with the trade deadline looming next Tuesday.

"I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said, per ESPN. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around.'"

Credit to Henry for sticking with his teammates through all the adversity.

#2782. Giants-Eagles matchup: How does QB Joe Milton change the equation?

The 4-2-1 New York Giants travel to Philadelphia this weekend to face the 2–6 Philadelphia Eagles, who enter the matchup on a six-game losing streak. Philadelphia is coming off a disappointing 27–10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football in Week 8.

Things are unraveling in Philadelphia. The Eagles are dealing with a rash of injuries and have switched from quarterback Tanner McKee to Joe Milton. Head coach Nick Sirianni is facing mounting questions from the media about offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, while general manager Howie Roseman has traded valuable assets in exchange for draft capital. To put it simply, things are far from sunny in Philadelphia.

Still, the Eagles will look to defend their home turf against a Giants franchise that hasn't won at Lincoln Financial Field since 2013. New York enters the matchup well-rested after its bye week, presenting an opportunity to snap that frustrating losing streak. And with the John Harbaugh era bringing a different identity and renewed expectations to the Giants, this team may finally have what it takes to change the narrative.

The Eagles' offense has struggled all season. Philadelphia ranks 30th in the league in points per game, with an average of just 17.1 points. They're 29th in total yards (2,122 yards), 32nd in yards per game (265 yards), and they're last in yards per play (4.4 YPP).

Philadelphia ranks 24th in passing yards per game (196.4) and 27th in rushing yards per game (88.1). They have a 37.3% third-down conversion rate, which ranks 26th in the league.

Tanner McKee has completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with a pair of touchdowns and interceptions. Joe Milton, though, poses a much different skill set that the Giants must account for. DeVonta Smith has missed a handful of games, including the loss to Washington last week; he still leads the team with 310 receiving yards.

Saquon Barkley is hobbled and played on a pitch count last week. He leads the Eagles with 274 rushing yards (4.9 YPC), with two rushing touchdowns. Elijah Mitchell is the backup running back with Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, and Dameon Pierce all on injured reserve.

Milton played three seasons at Michigan dating back to 2018 before he transferred to Tennessee. He threw for 2,813 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions and a 64.7% completion rate in Josh Heupel's offense back in 2023; he also rushed for 299 yards and seven touchdowns that year. Milton spent time with the Patriots, Cowboys, and now the Eagles.

Saquon Barkley played 32% of the snaps in Week 8. He touched the football often in his limited snaps over the last two weeks – he played 15% of snaps in Week 7. Mitchell is the primary backup now, and Jaydon Blue played 12% of snaps last week. The running situation – including the push up front from the line – has been poor.

Smith missed the last two weeks, and the two weeks prior to Week 6. Dontayvion Wicks hasn't played since Week 6. It's been the rookies, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper, who have played more than 90% of the snaps over the last two weeks. Both players have flashed.

Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore were the only other two wide receivers to play snaps against Washington, who operated heavier personnel packages without Smith. Tight end Dallas Goedert played 80% of the snaps, as Johnny Mundt and Eli Stowers both played 19% of snaps. Grant Calcaterra played 17% of snaps.

Jordan Mailata is the starting left tackle with rookie Markel Bell starting on the right side; Lane Johnson retired a few weeks ago, forcing Bell into the starting lineup. Tyler Steen mans the right guard spot, with Landon Dickerson playing left guard; Dickerson has been playing through a pectoral injury. Drew Kendall is the starting center now that Cam Jurgens is no longer an Eagle after he was traded to the Baltimore Ravens.

Starting Milton could provide the Eagles with a spark. The 6-foot-5, 245-pound quarterback is an excellent athlete with a howitzer arm, but he's bounced around practice squads and hasn't found consistency yet. Still, his mobility and strength in the pocket could allow him to escape the Giants' rush. It's an exciting move for Philadelphia — all things considered — but he's never proven consistent with timing, accuracy, and other nuances of the quarterback position, albeit he's just 26 years old.

New York has blitzed at a 36.6% rate this season, which ranks second only behind the Minnesota Vikings. I expect the Giants to dial up the pressure against the young quarterback, with a heavy middle-of-the-field closed approach. The Eagles have struggled offensively, but the Giants must focus on stopping Barkley when he is on the field.

The Giants can run man-to-man situational defense and focus on Cover-3, with a focus on stopping the run. Adjustments to middle-of-the-field-open defenses will happen in third-and-long situations. Fire-zone blitzes and a pre-snap loaded line of scrimmage should be employed in an attempt to force mistakes from the young quarterback.

New York's cornerbacks should press up on the line if Philadelphia attempts to run quick game often, as plenty of teams have attempted to run against the Giants. If pressure starts to get home on Milton and New York establishes a lead, the Giants can sit comfortably in zone to force check-downs underneath, as Washington did at the end of their win against Philadelphia.

If Philadelphia leans on more 12 personnel, especially with Eli Stowers, how do the Giants respond? Base or Nickel? Since New York will likely want to stop the run, they may respond with a heavier base package – five-man front. Philadelphia may look to try and get Stowers isolated against a linebacker or safety in those heavier tight end packages.

The Eagles' offensive line has been susceptible in both pass protection and as run blockers, relative to what we're accustomed to seeing every year. The Giants have to maintain the level of knock-back and physicality that they had against Houston. If they can do that, the Giants shouldn't have a problem winning the game.

The Giants are the better football team. Still, winning in Philadelphia hasn't been an easy venture for the Giants. I believe they get over the hump and win convincingly in Philadelphia. Pick: 30-13, Giants.

#2781. Sixers-Cavs by the numbers: Pressure, threes and a 29-point rematch

Sixers-Cavs by the numbers: Pressure, threes and a 29-point rematch originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers and Cavaliers have already played one game that looked like two.

Cleveland led by 29 points during the Sixers' home opener on Oct. 22 and carried a 69-45 advantage into halftime. Philadelphia responded by winning the second half, 69-37, and completing a 114-106 comeback.

It was the Sixers' largest comeback since the NBA began maintaining detailed play-by-play data in 1997-98. Only nine other teams during that span had overcome a deficit of at least 29 points.

Fifteen days later, the teams will meet again Friday night at Rocket Arena. This time, the matchup counts toward the NBA Cup standings.

The 8-1 Sixers have won five consecutive games and opened group play with a 98-93 victory over the Knicks. The 4-4 Cavs have dropped two straight and will make their Cup debut.

Here are five numbers that help frame the rematch.

Philadelphia's comeback required more than a hot shooting stretch.

The Sixers committed 15 turnovers in the first half, allowing Cleveland to build a 22-6 advantage in points off turnovers. Their pressure then changed the game after halftime.

The Cavs committed 21 turnovers by the end of the night. What had been a 16-point Cleveland advantage in points off turnovers finished even at 22 apiece.

"They upped their pressure and physicality," Cavs head coach Kenny Atkinson said after the game. "It was pretty clear. We did not handle it well."

The Sixers scored 64 of their 69 second-half points through their starting lineup. Tyrese Maxey finished with 28 points, and Philadelphia turned a game that appeared finished into a franchise-record comeback.

The first half of the opening meeting now looks like an exception.

The Sixers have committed 12.9 turnovers per 100 possessions this season, the NBA's second-lowest rate. They are also third in turnover differential, averaging 3.4 fewer giveaways than their opponents.

That is notable for a team that entered the season intending to play faster. Philadelphia has pushed the ball without routinely surrendering possessions.

LeBron James' presence as the primary facilitator has helped. So has Maxey's willingness to move the ball when defenses trap him. Joel Embiid has averaged 5.2 assists, third among qualified centers, and the Sixers have increasingly trusted VJ Edgecombe to make decisions late in games.

Cleveland's defense has not forced many mistakes. The Cavs enter Friday near the bottom of the league in opponent turnover rate.

The first meeting swung when the Sixers stopped giving away possessions and forced Cleveland into mistakes of its own.

The Sixers have allowed 105.1 points per 100 possessions, the NBA's second-best defensive rating. Cleveland enters with the league's ninth-ranked offense.

The Cavs are the only top-10 offense the Sixers have faced through their first nine games.

Philadelphia has held opponents to a 50 percent effective field-goal percentage and 31.8 percent shooting from three-point range. Its defensive shot profile has been encouraging, too. Only 46 percent of opposing three-point attempts have been classified as wide open, the fifth-lowest share in the league, and opponents have taken just 22 percent of their threes from the corners.

There is reason for caution. Based on the quality of shots Philadelphia has allowed, only Washington's opponents have underperformed their expected effective field-goal percentage by a wider margin. The Sixers have defended well, but opponents are unlikely to remain this cold indefinitely.

Cleveland, with Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Evan Mobley, can test whether those numbers hold against high-level individual shot creation.

The Cavs have attempted exactly 42 three-pointers per game and made 37.2 percent of them.

Cleveland went 7 for 29 from beyond the arc in Philadelphia. Mitchell, Harden and De'Andre Hunter combined to shoot 3 for 17. The Cavs scored 60 points in the paint and still reached 106, but their 24.1 percent performance from three prevented them from stopping the Sixers' comeback.

Friday's game could look considerably different if Cleveland generates its normal volume.

The Sixers have controlled the three-point line well so far, but Mitchell is coming off a 27-point performance against Oklahoma City and scored 32 in the first meeting with Philadelphia. Harden added 16 points that night, although his six turnovers became costly as the Sixers increased their pressure.

Philadelphia has been outrebounded by 5.1 per game. The Cavs rank sixth with 47.5 rebounds per contest.

The Sixers have already shown they can survive a major deficit on the glass. They beat Milwaukee by 11 despite getting outrebounded by 22. That is not a formula they will want to test regularly against Cleveland's size.

Mobley had 18 points and eight rebounds in the first meeting. Jarrett Allen added 14 points and seven boards, helping Cleveland win the rebounding battle, 46-44.

Whether Allen plays Friday remains uncertain.

Cleveland listed Allen as questionable because of a right knee injury after he left Wednesday's loss to Oklahoma City in the first quarter. Allen collided knee-to-knee with Thunder forward Chet Holmgren and did not return.

Allen's availability could significantly alter the matchup on the glass. If he sits, Thomas Bryant would likely handle more of the center minutes behind Mobley. If he plays, Cleveland will have the same starting frontcourt that outrebounded the Sixers during the first meeting.

Atkinson has emphasized the possession battle during Cleveland's two-game slide.

"You've got to get more shots than the other team," he said this week. "Rebounding is a big part of it."

That also carries added importance in the NBA Cup, where point differential is the second tiebreaker after head-to-head results.

Philadelphia enters Friday at 1-0 with a plus-five differential in East Group B. Miami is also 1-0 at plus-20, while Cleveland is playing its first group game.
