#2780. Clay Travis pushes back on Curt Cignetti’s claim ESPN favors the SEC

Curt Cignetti's accusation that ESPN's college football voices push the SEC drew a response Thursday from Clay Travis, the OutKick founder who now works as a Fox News contributor and hosts a weekly show on FS1. The Indiana Hoosiers coach made his case on his weekly radio show Wednesday, one day after the College Football Playoff selection committee released its first rankings of the season.

That first top 25 included 10 SEC teams and six from the Big Ten. Indiana debuted at No. 4 at 8-1, one spot ahead of a two-loss Alabama Crimson Tide team, while a 6-2 Iowa Hawkeyes team sat at No. 19.

"We Will Never See This Again": Analyst Stunned By Curt Cignetti's Historic Run After Hoosier's Big Ten Championship Image Via Instagram/@elitecollegefootball)

"Come on. These people, and there's a whole bunch of them, they march out of the tent, and they're given instructions on what to say, they follow the company line. Right, and I don't need to go any further. SEC gets a lot of love from the ESPN, you know, and all their writers that they don't technically pay but march to their drum. So that's why you see all these SEC teams up there, you know, and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten, not quite as high. But like I said, it's all going to be played out on the field," Cignetti said.

ESPN holds the SEC's national television rights and the rights to the College Football Playoff, and it aired Tuesday's rankings reveal. The rankings themselves come from the selection committee, so Cignetti's complaint is aimed at the noise around that room more than the room itself.

"Curt Cignetti says ESPN is biased toward the SEC. I disagree. In my entire media career, nobody has ever told me what I can or cannot do. Maybe the reason the SEC has so many teams ranked highly is because it's actually the best conference in college football," Travis wrote on X.

Travis answered a charge about ESPN with his own career, and he has never worked for ESPN. He has spent more than a decade at Fox, the Big Ten's lead television partner, and has been one of ESPN's most persistent critics for most of that time.

In October 2025, Travis reported on OutKick that ESPN had pulled Paul Finebaum from its programming after Finebaum discussed a possible U.S. Senate run in an interview with him. ESPN spokesman Bill Hofheimer publicly denied the report. Travis was alleging then the same kind of network control over ESPN talent that he is waving off now that Cignetti is the one alleging it.

Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti coaches his team against Ohio State Buckeyes in the third quarter during the football game in Columbus on Saturday, Nov. 23, 2024.

Ten SEC teams in the committee's top 25 is the best evidence for Travis' side of the conference argument, and the committee, not a network, put them there. At the top of the sport, the Big Ten owns the last three national championships through Michigan, Ohio State and Indiana. Cignetti's Hoosiers finished 16-0 last season and beat Alabama 38-3 in the Rose Bowl quarterfinal on the way, and no SEC team has played in the national title game since Georgia won it after the 2022 season.

Cignetti closed his remarks by saying it will all be played out on the field. For three straight Januarys, the field has sided with the Big Ten.

#2778. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2777. Ravens doomed by QB injuries, porous defense in loss to Jaguars

With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve, the Baltimore Ravens turned to Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UConn, to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.

The Ravens scraped their way through a 10-3 first quarter, but the Jaguars literally ran away with the game on a 50-yard Parker Washington touchdown just before halftime. A rainy night in Baltimore contributed to a sloppy second half that, to be frank, could have gotten much worse for the home team. Jacksonville ended up settling for three field goals inside the 30-yard line before another late touchdown – all on short fields – to finish with a 33-10 win.

Fagnano himself was playing with a heavily-bandaged right ankle that clearly limited his dropback capabilities. All of offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's tricks – motion, misdirection, even a healthy dose of Derrick Henry wildcat – could not cover up his quarterback's basic inability to plant on his back foot and drive the ball downfield. The Jaguars rolled out base personnel, loaded the box, and stuffed Henry for just 57 yards on 17 carries. Fagnano completed 10 of his 18 passes – most of them screens and other simple designed throws – for just 60 yards and two interceptions.

The Ravens' struggling offensive operation only compounded the issues. Doyle's trickery made execution even more of a priority for a unit that was playing its first full game with its best starting-five offensive line. But a slew of pre-snap penalties and missed blocks kept the offense behind the sticks and consistently killed their chances to sustain drives. Offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford in particular could be seen expressing his frustration at his unit on the sidelines. Outside of a 65-yard garbage-time rushing touchdown from Justice Hill, Baltimore managed just three points and 162 yards on 53 plays (3.05 yards per play).

Defensively, the Ravens picked up where they left off in recent games: on skates. The Jaguars marched down the field with little resistant on their opening drive, going 77 yards in just seven plays before punching in a goal-line touchdown. Baltimore's defense stiffened up after, but Washington's catch-and-run score was exactly the kind of back-breaking coverage collapse that has doomed the unit this year (and for the last few).

It was also exactly the kind of play that would doom a team trying to pull off an upset win with an undrafted rookie under center. A valiant second half – in which the Ravens defense twice forced three-and-out field goals after a Fagnano interception and kept the Jaguars out of the end zone until the game was effectively lost – deserves some mention, but there are no game balls in a defeated locker room. Regardless of the circumstances at quarterback, a team with a defensive-minded head coach; a respected defensive coordinator; an exciting young staff of defensive assistants; and one of the most expensive defensive rosters in football…should be able to play better defense. Standing tall on short fields in the second half means less after giving up a pair of full-length scores that effectively defined the game in the first. All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton also left the game with a hip injury and did not return, raising questions about the status of Baltimore's best defender for Week 10.

A 53-yard field goal from Jake Moody in his Ravens debut was an early highlight for a special teams unit that quickly fell into the same disarray as the team's other two phases. There is almost something impressive about Baltimore's ability to conjure up seemingly-obscure penalties like Rasheen Ali's illegal double-team block on a first-quarter return. And while a fourth-quarter comeback was never realistic, LaJohntay Wester's return fumble still added insult to injury and put an exhausted defense out on the field once again.

With Thursday's loss, the Ravens drop to 4-5, keeping them in last place in the AFC North. They have 10 days ahead of their next game, a Monday night matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. Jacoby Brissett should be in Baltimore by then, assuming Eric DeCosta finalizes the reported trade with the Arizona Cardinals. The 10-year veteran is no doubt an upgrade over Fagnano (not to mention his ankle), but he will face the same adverse circumstances, not to mention the heightened chance for procedural issues with a fourth quarterback under center.

If the Ravens' 2026 season is over, it did not end on a rainy Thursday night in Baltimore. It ended on a sunny afternoon in Buffalo, as soon as Jackson rushed off the field cradling his throwing hand. The loss to the Jaguars represents something different, arguably worse: just how bad things can get.

#2775. Niko Kovač: Jobe Bellingham has “fully deserved” first England call-up

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham has received his first call-up to the England senior squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, BVB head coach Niko Kovač reflected on the 21-year-old's selection, which will give him the opportunity to represent England alongside his older brother, Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham.

"He has truly deserved it. The progress he has made has been tremendous. He has invested a lot of effort and works extremely hard. And the way he has gone about things this year has been excellent. "He should keep going, and I'm convinced he will, because he has a tremendous attitude, loves what he does, and has everything it takes to become a truly great player."

Jobe Bellingham joined Borussia Dortmund from Sunderland in the summer of 2025. He has made 14 appearances for BVB this season, including 10 starts.

#2772. Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1

Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls.

All five of the Sixers' starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds.

VJ Edgecombe's 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards.

Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of "right foot plantar fascia injury management." He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers' win over the Hornets.

"Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. "They're just trying to manage it. It's very painful, if you've ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we're just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can."

Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that's sidelined him to start the season.

"He's been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around," Nurse said. "I think they want to get to tomorrow's appointment. Hopefully, it'll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit."

The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday:

After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis' hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team's first field goal.

Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James' long-distance feeds were a major asset.

"If you're open, he's going to pass it," Edgecombe said of James. "The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get 'em. If you're open and he sees you, he's going to pass the ball."

Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers' explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13.

The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he's already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won't become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers' enhanced star power.

Over the team's first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting.

Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later.

Bona remained the Sixers' main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers' victory over the Bucks, posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It's reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five.

The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona's first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield.

The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead.

Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points.

The Bulls cut the Sixers' lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn't needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes.

Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star's health is clearly not close to 100 percent.

"I was on a minutes restriction," he said. "(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It's painful. Just got to manage it.

"If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We've been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs."

The Sixers' lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6.

As for the Sixers, they'll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings.

"You've got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent," Nurse said. "A lot of these teams play a way that's a little scary. It's fast and it's furious, lots of threes. … They're going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they're not easy games and I'm glad that we handled it professionally tonight."

#2771. Dolphins news: Lions game preview, trade rumors continue, Ollie Gordon’s penalty

The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions on Sunday in Week 9 of the NFL season. The game features a Miami team in the midst of a reset and hoping to see continued growth from a roster with 14 rookies and seven more first-year players. On the other side, the Lions come into the game hoping to prove they are back to being contenders for a deep NFC playoff run after settling for last place in the NFC North last year.

The Lions could serve as the example for Miami and their reset goals. The Lions underwent a massive reset in 2021, the first year under head coach Dan Campbell. Since a 3-13-1 season to start his tenure, Campbell has led the Lions to a winning record in each of the last four years, going 9-8 in 2022, 12-5 in 2023, 15-2 in 2024, and 9-8 last year, despite the fourth-place finish in the division. The Lions won the NFC North in 2023 and 2024 and advanced to the NFC Championship game in 2023. So far this season, Detroit is 5-2 and looking like they are headed to another winning season.

#2768. NFL predictions: Health is once again the story for the Panthers in Week 9

The Carolina Panthers are down at least their top two, possibly their top four corners again this week. At corner, Will Lee III and Marco Wilson may form a more competent cornerback duo than one would expect for their original places on the depth chart at the start of the season (third string and on the street, respectively).

The Broncos are another team looking to find their rushing game against the Panthers. #2767. ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers

'I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jaylen Brown has spent the opening weeks of the season describing the Sixers as a work in progress.

He offered a similarly humble perspective Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His performance, however, provided the clearest look yet at how he can influence this group while sharing the floor with the club's other established stars.

Brown finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists in the Sixers' 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. He shot 9 for 15 from the field, made four three-pointers and did not commit a turnover.

Five of his rebounds came on the offensive end, an area Brown has emphasized while the Sixers continue piecing together their frontcourt rotation.

"Just a mindset," Brown said. "Just trying to create extra opportunities for my team. As we're trying to patch together our fives and our front line, I try to make an extra contribution and emphasis on the glass."

Brown has also been careful about how he describes his place on a roster that already belonged to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter Monday, continuing his torrid start to the season. He has led the Sixers in scoring while being the only starter to appear in all eight games.

Brown is not interested in interrupting that.

"Maxey's been leading the way, 100 percent," Brown said. "He's been here. This is his team. Him and Joel have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to complement those guys. I'm finding my footing, but Maxey has been leading the way for sure."

Brown's footing looked firm against Chicago.

Beyond his scoring, he helped the Sixers control the glass, moved the ball within an offense that generated 23 assists during the first half and supplied the physicality Nick Nurse expects from him.

"The dude is tough and he wins," Nurse said. "I'll take that all day long. The degree of difficulty on some of the shots he hit was really amazing. I thought he pounded the glass and got some key rebounds. Makes a lot of winning plays. Man, he's a winner."

Brown spent the first 10 years of his career in Boston. He won a championship there, reached another NBA Finals and grew from a 20-year-old prospect into one of the league's premier two-way wings.

Moving into a new system alongside James, Embiid and Maxey was never going to be seamless.

"I mean, he's fitting in along with all of us," James said. "We're getting better and better. It's not going to happen overnight. He spent his first 10 years in a system in Boston, in the city, so it's going to take some adjustment.

"It takes adjustment for him. It's going to take adjustment for the rest of the guys that joined this franchise as well. But tonight was a great step."

James pointed to Brown's "pressure, his shot-making ability, his rebounding ability" and his professionalism.

Brown's early influence has extended beyond his production.

The Sixers entered Monday with one of the NBA's best half-court defenses. Brown has been one of the group's most persistent voices, stressing communication, preparation and attention to opposing players' tendencies.

"That's the part that I care about the most as a group, not individually," Brown said. "Having a mentality night in and night out, respecting your opponent, respecting the game, making sure that we are executing our coverages, we're being clear in our communication and then we're also taking away tendencies on a night-to-night basis.

"Those things I just explained are over 50 percent of the battle."

Brown understands that maintaining those details across an 82-game schedule will require more than reminders.

"A little bit of accountability," he said. "You learn different guys require different things. How you communicate with each guy may be a little different, but accountability for sure and confrontation if need be.

"The offense is going to be what it's going to be, but our defense has got to be non-negotiable. That's something I say all the time. Non-negotiable. You want to be a good team, defense is non-negotiable."

The Sixers showed both sides of their defensive potential Monday.

They built a double-digit lead during the first half, allowed Chicago to score 36 points in the second quarter and then created separation after halftime. Philadelphia held the Bulls to 20 points in the third quarter before pulling away in the fourth.

Brown did not celebrate their ability to raise their intensity after it slipped.

"I don't like that we have that," he said. "It's good that we have shown the potential, but we've got to keep that switch on. It doesn't work like that where you just flip the switch.

"It can catch up to us and it can bite us against a better team or on a night that we're not being as crisp on offense. It can't be a switch just because we're playing a lesser opponent or whatever the case may be. We've got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to end. Can't skip any steps."

That urgency accompanies considerable optimism.

Brown said the Sixers enjoy playing together. He loves when James grabs a rebound because "he's like a quarterback," capable of launching an outlet pass or immediately pushing the pace.

The group is learning when to attack, when to move the ball and how to avoid hesitating in its effort to play unselfishly.

"It's a lot of talent, man," Brown said. "We like each other, and we're just kind of building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. I think we're taking steps forward every single day."

The Sixers are 7-1 despite Brown believing those steps remain incomplete. They have won close games, erased sizable deficits and received important contributions from different players.

Brown's performance Monday showed another version of how their pieces can fit.

"We still have a long way to go to being a really, really solid, great team," Brown said. "But we've been able to win some games. We started out the season great, 7-1, and you haven't seen our best version yet.

#2763. Scouting the Enemy: Carolina Panthers

The Denver Broncos will battle Carolina Panthers on Sunday. It's a huge matchup for the Broncos who have a shot to keep their winning streak alive and enter their bye week with a 7-2 record if they are victorious. Here is a deeper look at their Week 9 opponent.

2025 Carolina Panthers Regular Season Review

The Carolina Panthers won the NFC South with an 8-9 record in Head Coach Dave Canales' second season leading the team.. They lost to the Los Angeles Rams in the Wild Card Round 34-31.

2026 Carolina Panthers Offseason Additions and Departures

After securing their first division title since the 2017 season, the Carolina Panthers made a few big splashes in free agency to be more competitive in 2026. The two high-profile signings came on defense. They signed edge rusher Jaelan Phillips to a four-year, $120 million dollar contract. The Panthers also inked All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd to a three-year, $45 million dollar contract.

Carolina didn't have many big-named departures. However, they parted ways with two starters. Defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson and offensive lineman Austin Corbettt, whose time with the Panthers was marred by injuries.

In the 2026 NFL Draft, they made bolstering their trenches a priority. They took Georgia tackle Monroe Freeling in the first round and Texas Tech defensive tackle Lee Hunter in the second. Both have been starters for them this season. Tennessee wide receiver Chris Brazzell II was their third-round pick. Unfortunately, his rookie season ended early after suffering a torn LCL in summer.

On the bright side, their Day 3 group of talent has earned plenty of playing time. They snagged two starters on Day 3 with Texas A&M cornerback Will Lee and Penn State safety Zakee Wheatley. Fifth-round offensive lineman Sam Hecht and seventh-round linebacker Jackson Kuwatch have earned backup roles and are playing on special teams for them this season.

Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Bryce Young

As noted above, the Panthers made improving their defense a big part of their free agent plans. On offense, they banked on the progression of quarterback Bryce Young to be the catalyst that would take their offense to the next level. He is my X-Factor for them on offense.

It's been an up-and-down season for Young. Even so, the Panthers have had a big turnaround on offense. They are a Top 10 unit in the NFL by most metrics. Wide receivers Tetairoa McMillian and Jalen Coker have been very productive. Tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller have gotten their fair share of looks in the passing game too.

Young has done a great job diving up his targets and despite a less-than-optimal completion percentage. In seven starts, Young is completing 59-percent of his passes, thrown for 1,921 yards, 13 touchdowns, and has just 5 interceptions on the season. He is doing great on first down and is moving the chains early and often. However, his third down efficiency has been less than optimal.

A big reason for that is poor play from their offensive line. In just seven games, Young has been sack almost as many times as he was in 2025. This is a game where Denver's defensive front seven needs to make an impact. While their sack total isn't nearly as good as it was last season, they're still a top-ranked team when it comes to generating pressure and getting quarterback hits. If they can rattle Young, I like Denver's odds of winning this game.

Defensive X-Factor: Linebacker Devin Lloyd

The Panthers made some splashes in free agency to upgrade their defense. Alas, it has been their biggest weakness to date. No excuses can be made, but they have had a bunch of injuries. Their poor play and inconsistency led to the firing of Ejiro Evero at the end of October. Broncos Country may remember that name, as Evero was the Defensive Coordinator for the Broncos in 2022 when Nathaniel Hackett was Head Coach.

One bright spot for them on defense has been linebacker Devin Lloyd. He's my X-Factor for them on defense. Lloyd had a Pro-Bowl and All-Pro season in his fourth and final year with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. He notched 135 tackles, 5 interceptions, and 1.5 sacks.

This season, he has continued to play at a high level. The fifth-year pro already has 69 tackles, 2 interceptions, and 2 sacks on the season. If there is any player on defense Denver's offense needs to be cognizant of, it's Lloyd. He has incredible range and playmaking ability. Whether it's against the run or the pass, he is one of the league's most versatile defenders that can make a huge impact on the game.

How the Broncos can achieve a victory over the Panthers

ICYMI: Yesterday, I wrote how the Broncos can achieve their seventh victory of the season over the Panthers. Overall, this is a game where I really like Denver's chances. If they can establish the run on offense and get after Young defensively, they should be able to come away with a big win before the bye week.

Hart's Prediction: Broncos 30, Panthers 17.

#2762. Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30

Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers remain the Eastern Conference's sole leader.

They earned a 112-106 road win over the Pistons on Wednesday night to move to 8-1 on the season and stay at the top of the standings. Detroit fell to 6-2.

The Sixers last started 8-1 in the 2023-24 season, which was Nick Nurse's first as the team's head coach.

Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 30 points and pulled down seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid had 26 points and a season-best 15 rebounds. LeBron James posted 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Tyrese Maxey added 19 points and seven assists.

The Pistons' leading scorers were Duncan Robinson with 27 points and Cade Cunningham with 26.

The Sixers were down Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pistons' injured players included Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion).

Nurse told reporters in Detroit he thinks "it'll be another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear (Barlow) for getting on the court to see where he is," according to Sixers Wire's Ky Carlin.

The Sixers will visit the Cavaliers on Friday night. Here are observations on their victory over Detroit:

Embiid assisted the Sixers' first basket with a sharp pass out of a double team. He saw Brown's cut along the baseline and dished to him for a layup.

Detroit ran several double drag screen actions early, forcing Embiid to defend on the perimeter. The Pistons started 7 for 11 from the floor and took a 17-11 edge on a Robinson three-pointer.

The Sixers then made a 10-0 run and Embiid was right in the middle of it. He converted a put-back layup after a pretty high-low feed from James. Embiid hit two foul shots to give the Sixers the lead. The team raised its defensive level and Detroit's offense grew frigid.

Embiid was very good on the glass in the first half, grabbing eight rebounds. The Sixers had an excellent rebounding game as a team, limiting the Pistons to four offensive boards over 48 minutes.

Embiid didn't break out of his early-season three-point shooting slump, going 0 for 3. He's 3 for 26 (11.5 percent) on the season and hasn't made a three since the Sixers' second game.

Late in the second quarter, Embiid got into a dead-ball dust-up with Tolu Smith. After an officials' review, Embiid was assessed a technical foul for "initiating" the altercation.

Playing on his 26th birthday, Maxey missed his first four field goals and was scoreless until he hit a floater with 31.5 seconds left in the first quarter.

Brown picked up the scoring slack, tallying 10 points in the first on 4-for-6 shooting and hitting a deep, buzzer-beating three to put the Sixers up 29-21. He produced at all three levels, chose smart spots to attack and looked comfortable in the rhythm of the Sixers' offense.

Meanwhile, James did his usuall stellar work as a passer. He assisted two Adem Bona slams in the second quarter and constantly spotted open teammates. Nurse rewarded Bona's strong opening stint, playing him for a lengthy stretch.

Brown swished a corner triple to extend the Sixers' lead to 48-31. With a 3-for-5 night, Brown is at 45.7 percent from long distance so far this season. It wouldn't be surprising at all if Brown's three-point shooting improved from last season's 34.7 percent clip. With such an abundance of star power, the Sixers' hope will be that everyone gets regular open looks beyond the arc throughout the year.

As for Maxey, he sat with 3:26 left in the second quarter after being whistled for his third foul. Even with a mere two points from Maxey, the Sixers entered halftime holding a 14-point advantage.

The Pistons played better basketball to begin the third quarter.

Following a John Collins alley-oop jam, Nurse called timeout with his team's lead down to single digits. The Pistons' offense sustained some success, but the Sixers prevented a sustained run.

Embiid played an especially physical, aggressive third quarter. He tipped in his own miss and Maxey then sunk a three to make the Sixers' lead 84-68. They were up as many as 17 points in the third.

Embiid sat out the fourth quarter Monday night for the Sixers' win over the Bulls and said he was on a minutes restriction (25) because of his right foot plantar fasciitis. He played the fourth period against the Pistons and logged 33 minutes. Bona went back to the locker room early in the fourth. Nurse told reporters postgame that Bona had "neck soreness."

Detroit did not let the Sixers coast to victory.

Robinson drained a three. Cunningham made a pair of free throws and drove in for a layup that cut the Pistons' deficit to 106-102.

The Sixers halted the Pistons' run before anything disastrous was on the table. Brown blocked a Cunningham three-point try, Embiid knocked down two foul shots, and the East's No. 1 early-season team improved to 4-0 on the road.

#2758. LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it

LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top.

In the third quarter of the Sixers' 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he'd take fan interaction to a whole new level.

James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments.

It wasn't until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn't hold back giving reporters a play-by-play.

"I spilled some of his wine," he said postgame. "I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright."

Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN.

"[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said 'My bad,' my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court]."

"At the end of the day he's another man like me," Clemons said. "I mean he's LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it's nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though."

It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans' cups, but it's rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks' court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan's beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate.

If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having.

The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season.

"It's a long marathon. And if you don't find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you're working and even though you're locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us."

Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old's mindset coming into the season.

"This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it's his] 24th year. It's a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he's a big part of that."

The vibes are high. It's difficult for them not to be.

With Monday's win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They've won four in a row and the only team they've lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

#2756. Detroit Lions LB Devin White closing in on return from broken forearm

The Detroit Lions could be getting some reinforcements back at the linebacker position soon.

Devin White, who broke his right forearm in the Lions' Week 5 win over the Arizona Cardinals, is scheduled to have updated imaging on his arm next week and told the Free Press he could play again as soon as this month.

"We're ramping it up now, so I think it's just roll with it right now and whenever they feel like I'm ready – mentally I'm going to be ready, so it's just whenever physically I'm able to perform at the level they want me to, I'll be ready," he said. "I'm going headfirst."

The Lions lost linebackers Jack Campbell (neck) and Jimmy Rolder (hamstring) to serious injuries last week and shuffled personnel at the position in recent days.

Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske are expected to join Derrick Barnes in the starting lineup for this week's game against the Miami Dolphin., Barnes will handle the green-dot defensive communication responsibilities in Campbell's absence, and the Lions promoted Joe Bachie from the practice squad, signed K.J. Britt off the New England Patriots practice squad and added Owen Pappoe to the practice squad.

RELATED: Lions players breathe 'sigh of relief' at latest Jack Campbell update

White, a one-time Pro Bowler with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers who signed with the Lions in training camp, played as a rotational third linebacker the first five weeks of the season. He had three tackles in 18 snaps in a Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints, played a season-high 33 snaps in a Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills, then was out of the lineup the next two weeks before returning to play 16 snaps against the Cardinals before he was injured on a friendly-fire play from teammate Chuck Clark.

"It's crazy, man," White said. "I get all the way to Year 8 and first time ever being on IR. And stuff was going good, but I mean, just a good mindset to get back."

Asked if he was bummed he wouldn't be able to play against his old team the Buccaneers later this month, White said, "I hope I do [get to play against them]."

"I don't know [if I'll be back by then], but I hope," he said.

After this week's game against the Dolphins, the Lions travel to Germany to play the New England Patriots, host the Bucs the following week on Nov. 22 and play the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving.

"I'm doing really good on my way back," White said. "I think mentally being away from the game, it makes you love it even more and appreciate even more. So I think me coming back is going to feel real good, and I'm just thankful that I will have an opportunity to come back and help this team because I feel like this team has a great window as far as doing some major things. And I don't want to get ahead of myself, but it's a great team, one of the greatest offenses I've been around, and defense, all we got to do is just limit people to under 19 and we got a great shot of winning ball games."

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2754. Defending champion Nasa Hataoka takes one-stroke lead after two rounds at Japan Classic

OMITAMA, Japan — Defending champion Nasa Hataoka eagled the par-5 17th for a back-nine 30 and an 8-under 64 to take a one-stroke lead Friday after two rounds of the LPGA Tour's Toto Japan Classic.

Hataoka, who won in a playoff last year in a rain-shortened tournament, had a 36-hole total of 12-under 132 Friday.

Miyu Yamashita, who won last week's Maybank Championship in Malaysia, pulled her tee shot on the 18th fairway which resulted in her only bogey of the day to shoot 67 and was in second place.

Ana Belac, who became the first Slovenian player on the LPGA Tour in 2021, was tied for third after a 65 with Fuka Suga (67), two strokes behind.

Belac had eight birdies Friday and only earned her spot in the field when Ariya Jutanugarn withdrew on Monday with an undisclosed injury.

Hataoka, who has five top-10 finishes this season, grew up not far from the Taiheiyo Club Minori Course northeast of Tokyo.

"I don't have a chance to play in front of so many Japanese fans, so I was really happy to be playing so well today," Hataoka said through an interpreter.

The Japan Classic is the last of four tournaments on the LPGA's so-called late-season Asian swing.

Ruoning Yin made a four-foot birdie putt on the 16th hole and won the LPGA Shanghai by one stroke on Oct. 18 to start the swing. In the second tournament a week later in South Korea, Yuri Yoshida won at Pine Beach Golf Links, her first LPGA Tour victory.

#2753. Doc Rivers shares criticisms of Giannis Antetokounmpo's game − and how he can improve

If you ask Doc Rivers, Giannis Antetokounmpo is in the perfect place to take the next step in his career.

In the most recent episode of "The Bill Simmons Podcast," Rivers dished on his time with the Milwaukee Bucks, how he navigated the ill-fated Damian Lillard trade and the highs and lows that came with coaching the Greek Freak.

"I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude," Rivers told Simmons. "He's interesting. He's not easy. He plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy because he has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way. Downhill. Force, force. Every play, he wants to force it."

The number one thing Rivers emphasized was execution. Preparing the right way and setting his teammates up for success is the area the Hall of Fame coach believes Antetokounmpo fell short in during their time together. But now, with Antetokounmpo on the Miami Heat under Erik Spoelstra, Rivers is hopeful that will come to fruition.

"I wish he learned how to execute better," Rivers said. "He's one of those guys − you get a lot of them from the U.S., AAU guys − that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team. And I told Giannis this, the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shootarounds to lock in on execution. And now he has a coach who is as good as there is in execution."

Antetokounmpo landed in South Beach this summer after a blockbuster trade that put an end to the long-running standoff between the 10-time All-Star and the Bucks front office, but it's been anything but greener pastures early on. The Heat are 3-6 in their first nine games despite him averaging 28.3 points and 12.5 rebounds a night.

The Golden State Warriors pulled away from a tie game against Miami at halftime to earn a comfortable 120-100 win Thursday, thanks in no small part to the ability of Draymond Green, Al Horford and Charles Bassey to contain Antetokounmpo to just one point in seven fourth quarter minutes down the stretch.

#2749. Warriors vs. Heat player grades: Steph Curry explodes as the bench steps up

The Golden State Warriors are officially rolling. With Thursday night's 120-100 win over the Miami Heat, the Dubs have won six games in a row, and their 0-3 start is a distant memory.

Thursday was a game they were expected to win — Miami is off to a sluggish start, and played an overtime game the night before — and win they did, though they once came out of the gates slowly, trailing by 10 early and entering halftime with a tied score. But a win is a win is a win, and a 20-point win is a 20-point win is a 20-point win.

So let's grade the players who got the job done. As always, grades are based on my expectations of each player, with a "B" grade representing the average performance for that player.

Note: True-shooting percentage (TS) is a scoring efficiency metric that accounts for threes and free throws. Entering Thursday's games, league-average TS was 57.1%.

16 minutes, 10 points, 2 assists, 1 block, 1 turnover, 1 foul, 4-for-6 shooting, 2-for-4 threes, 83.3% TS, -5

Richard got another start, presumably partially due to Gui Santos' absence, and partially due to wanting to get a strong defender on the court against Andrew Wiggins. Richard played awesomely against Wiggins, who shot just 1-for-6 on the day, and also when taking turns on Klay Thompson.

When the Warriors were struggling to start the game, Richard was also the team's lone source of offense … not only was he the first player on the team to reach double digits, but he was the only Dub with double digits at the half.

It's unfair that Richard ended up with a -5 plus/minus on a night where the Warriors won by 20. That's really just the result of him being one of their best players when they were struggling, and then not getting much second-half playing time due to other players heating up. So it goes. They got the win, he played well, and I'm sure he's quite happy with all of it.

Grade: A-Post-game bonus: Worst plus/minus on the team.

30 minutes, 17 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists, 3 steals, 1 block, 2 turnovers, 4 fouls, 6-for-14 shooting, 1-for-3 threes, 4-for-6 free throws, 51.1% TS, -1

Lendeborg — in just the ninth game of his career — has reached the point where you feel like he had a quiet game and then look at the box score and he's sitting on a 17-8-6-3-1 line. Ridiculous!

His NBA crash course continued, as he opened up the game defending Bam Adebayo, and had plenty of possessions against Giannis Antetokounmpo as well. Both of those players had pretty decent numbers, but I was impressed with the job that Lendeborg did when lined up against them.

It wasn't his most efficient shooting night, but we're likely going to see that more and more as he's given a larger and larger role in the offense. Both his efficiency and his plus/minus were hurt by the fact that Steve Kerr trusts Lendeborg to be The Man when Steph Curry and Draymond Green sit … and sometimes when they're on the court, too. As a result, he doesn't always have a ton of help, and there were plenty of shots in this game that he missed because he was the last-second bail-out option. Comes with the territory.

Ultimately, a very strong game for Lendeborg, and one where we really saw him start to further his chemistry with other players on the team, such as Charles Bassey and Brandon Williams.

Grade: B+Post-game bonus: Led the team in rebounds.

27 minutes, 2 points, 5 rebounds, 11 assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 3 turnovers, 1 foul, 1-for-3 shooting, 0-for-2 threes, 33.3% TS, +13

Green's patience on offense continues to shine through this year. He's played in seven games this season and only shot the ball 21 times, total. A large part of that is the presence of Lendeborg, who simply makes the offense work much better, and gives the team another 20-point scorer. But part of it is Draymond showing restraint on that end of the court. There will be a time and a place for him to take a lot of shots and score a lot of points, but it is very noticeable how much more fluid the offense is with him acting solely as a facilitator (both with and without the ball).

The season-high 11 assists for Green were a joy to watch, and it was the driving force for the 36 team assists the Dubs had, which was also a season high.

But above all else, this game was a reminder as to the value Green brings on the defensive end, not just through his actions on any given possession, but his abilities that allow Kerr flexibility when game-planning. On paper, Green being the starting center against an opposing frontcourt of Antetkounmpo and Adebayo is a bit silly, but his talent and versatility makes it work.

Grade: APost-game bonus: Led the team in assists.

32 minutes, 9 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 1 turnover, 3 fouls, 3-for-8 shooting, 2-for-6 threes, 1-for-2 free throws, 50.7% TS, +5

It's always a special day when Klay returns to the Bay Area. But when he does, it's hard to ignore the storyline of his departure, even if it's long been buried. A lot went into the Warriors legend deciding to leave the team, but much of it stemmed from being upset at Podziemski starting to take Thompson's spot in the starting lineup, and the way the franchise handled that shift.

While it's easy to understand and empathize with Klay, it's also pretty apparent that the Warriors made the right move. Thompson is headed for the Hall of Fame, but these days Podziemski is certainly the better — and more complete — player.

That was on display Thursday night, even though it wasn't Podz's best game, by the stat sheet or by the eye test. He struggled to get separation against Miami's length, but he played awesome defense and made things happen all over the court.

28 minutes, 29 points, 1 rebound, 4 assists, 1 steal, 1 foul, 9-for-19 shooting, 6-for-12 threes, 5-for-5 free throws, 68.4% TS, +17

Curry was something of a non-factor in the first half. He looked like he simply didn't have it, and shot just 2-for-10 from the field. After the game, Kerr mentioned that one of the most special things about Curry is his ability to bounce back from a bad performance while it's still happening, instead of needing to wait for the next game.

And my goodness was that exemplified in this contest. On the other side of the court was Antetokounmpo, a recent MVP, and Adebayo, who has the second-highest scoring game in NBA history to his name. Yet once the second half began, the contest emphatically belonged to Curry, who was far and away the best player on the court. He truly took over. And thanks to the addition of Lendeborg and the depth of this team, it seems like Curry will be able to do that more and more often this year, given that he doesn't have to expend all his energy carrying the team on his shoulders all the time.

He's still averaging more than a point per minute, and he's under two turnovers per game. The end, I'm pleased to report, is not in sight.

It turns out that having three rest days — Horford didn't play on Monday — is a superpower for Big Al. That probably shouldn't be surprising, considering that this is his 20th NBA season. Against an incredibly athletic team, Horford more than held his own, with elite interior defense and a slick jumper that proved pivotal in the second-half rally.

He remains a savvy and trustworthy veteran on his worst day, and a two-way impact player on his best.

Grade: APost-game bonus: Best plus/minus on the team.

Not the best offensive night for Melton, but it was a fantastic game for him on the other end of the court. His defense has been so strong this year and, just as importantly, his hands have been so active, which helps create healthy chaos. Critically, Melton has been one of — if not the — best player on the team at turning defense into offense this year. It feels like every time he gets a steal he pushes the ball in transition, and every time he gets a deflection, he leaks out for a teammate to find him. The Dubs had 28 points off of turnovers in this game (an 11-point advantage, despite only forcing one more turnover than they committed), and Melton was a big reason why, even if he only put one shot through the hoop.

Great defense, bad offense? We'll call it a wash.

I'm having so much fun watching Williams on the Warriors. He's just such an enjoyable player to watch, and he plays in a way that's been so foreign to the Dubs over the last decade-plus. Good things happen when Williams is on the court, and specifically when he has the ball in his hands. After so much movement of Curry dancing around the perimeter and cutting baseline to baseline, defenses seem completely confused when Williams gets on the court and starts exploding downhill like prime Frank Gore hitting a gap.

He's been a little inconsistent this year in terms of actually finishing, but good things happen regardless, simply by nature of attacking. In this game, however? No problem finishing whatsoever, or dishing to open teammates. He even blocked a pair of shots! A tremendous game for a vital spark plug.

Niang is really starting to show up as advertised, and then some. We expected we'd get a heady veteran who made smart plays and drained threes, and that's arriving in spades. What we didn't expect was to get someone who was going to provide such fiery leadership. That was once again on display Thursday, when Niang did something that not many players are willing to do: go nose-to-nose with Bobby Portis Jr.

The forward had a few choice words for Portis while they shoved their foreheads against each other like bucks during mating season. You could see the trash-talking venom in Niang's eyes, and both players were awarded technicals.

It's fight and intensity that the Warriors need, especially with Jimmy Butler III sidelined. And it's also a healthy complement to Green, as Niang is willing to scuffle with anyone — this was his third such instance of the season — but stops short of crossing the line. His teammates really seem to feed off of it.

Fear not, Warriors fans. Kerr has heard your complaints, logged them, and taken action. After this game, Kerr said that Bassey is "earning more minutes for sure," so you can expect him to get larger chunks of minutes going forward.

This wasn't a perfect game from the energetic big. He got a little too careless, which led to three turnovers and five fouls in just 14 minutes. And he lost his perfect shooting night when he hoisted a victory cigar three that badly missed.

But just because he wasn't perfect doesn't mean he wasn't damn good, and Bassey was exactly that: damn good. He's not only figuring out how to finish more effectively, but building up great chemistry with his teammates. His defense is so much better than it was earlier in his career, as he's genuinely turned a liability into an asset, and it comes with a bunch of rebounds, too.

#2748. England boss Tuchel: Bellingham brothers are an ‘incredible story’

England boss Thomas Tuchel hailed the "incredible story" of Jude and Jobe Bellingham being named in the senior squad together for the first time.

Jobe, who is two years younger than his big brother, has been handed a maiden call-up to Tuchel's 25-man squad for next week's Nations League matches with Croatia and Spain.

If Jobe makes his debut, the pair would become the 22nd set of brothers to play for England's senior team, with Jude previously saying it would be the "biggest dream of my life" to share a pitch with his sibling for his country.

That could become a reality after Tuchel promoted the younger brother from the Under-21s squad following an impressive start to the campaign with Borussia Dortmund, with Jude celebrating the call-up by posting a picture on Instagram of the pair wearing Birmingham City shirts when they were younger.

"It's an incredible achievement for the family and for the brothers to be both nominated for their national team, which is an incredible story in itself," Tuchel said.

"Like I said, I was very happy to give him the call up, and I saw his excitement straight away, and his smile.

"He's a very open and calm personality. So it was a very nice phone call, of course, because it was very good news.

"We see him in central midfield, so he's one of five players now for the central midfield.

"He's a more defensive player than his brother Jude, so strong on the ball, good physique, big body, very physical player, and can keep possession.

"So now it's on him because we only have basically Tuesday and Wednesday to prepare for the Thursday match [against Croatia].

"It's now up to him but he's of course excited and happy and eager to impress and that's the best foundation to have a good camp for us."

Jobe's call-up comes after injury to Alex Scott, Kobbie Mainoo's omission and the fact Myles Lewis-Skelly is suspended for Thursday's match with Croatia.

"First of all, Lee [Carsley] is speaking very, very highly of him in the 21s," Tuchel added.

"He's a standout player for a long time now. He's the captain of the Under-21s, so, I think the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time.

"And that's what Jobe has done. On top of it, he found his way and found his rhythm with Dortmund. He has had an excellent start to the season. He's a regular starter now there and very influential."

Fulham winger Josh King also receives a maiden call-up, having been part of the pre-World Cup camp in Florida.

"He's just a fantastic character, he made a big impression in the US, and then he had a good start to the season," the German added.

"Now he gives us a bit of flexibility. He can play all four offensive positions."

Elsewhere, Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer and Manchester United midfielder Mainoo were high-profile omissions, with Djed Spence and Ben White brought into a 25-man squad that defender Nico O'Reilly dropped out of.

Declan Rice returns after injury, but Bukayo Saka is absent with a thigh injury and Tuchel decided not to bring in Noni Madueke as his Arsenal team-mate's replacement.

#2746. Warriors defense erases Heat big men in second half as Golden State wins 6th in a row

It's hard to know what Steph Curry has been doing during halftime this season. Maybe he's snacking on popcorn. Maybe he's firing himself up by reading internet comments. Maybe Steph is getting pep talks over FaceTime from Natalie Nakase.

Regardless of what he's doing — meditation, yoga, writing letters complaining about affordable housing projects, watching highlights from Season 2 of "Holey Moley" — it's working. Curry shot 4-of-5 from the field, sank three three-pointers, and scored 14 points in the 3rd quarter as the Golden State Warriors outscored the Miami Heat 38-23. The game was tied at halftime, and the Dubs went on to win by 20, with a tidy final score of 120-100.

Curry is now averaging nearly 12 points in third quarters. He's shooting 62.2% from the field and 65% behind the arc and hasn't missed a third-quarter free throw all season. He finished Thursday's game with 29 points, four assists, and six more three-pointers, and has made at least five triples in each of his last four games.

The Warriors won their sixth straight game after starting the season 0-3. They took the victory Thursday night at the expense of two of their old teammates, Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson. Wiggins scored just two points, while Captain Klay had 11 points, though he did block two shots. The two former champions combined to shoot 4-for-16 from the field, while Thompson didn't look amused by his Splash Brother clowning around for a photo during the game.

It's tough for those guys, in part because the Heat's warmups for Thursday's game were black shirts with a red flames on the back. It feels like the team let Guy Fieri and the assistant manager of a Hot Topic have final say on the design. It simply doesn't look good for basketball players in their 30's to dress like they're part of a UFC fighter's entourage.

Giannis Antetokounmpo was a constant Warriors trade target before forcing his way to Miami this summer, where it's not going great. He's averaging 28.3 points and 12.5 rebounds but his team is 3-6. Antetokounmpo had 20 points and 14 rebounds in the loss, but most of that production happened in the first half. After halftime, the Greek Freak had four points and four rebounds and took only four shots, clearly frustrated by Draymond Green's defense.

Green scored two points but delivered 11 assists and finished +13 with a steal and a block. Anecdotally, Green's beard also looks darker, which could have been the NBC Sports Bay Area picture quality, but we think it's possible that Draymond is using BED's (Beard Enhancing Drugs).

During one sequence in the second quarter, Green and Curry took turns feeding rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who filled up the box score with 17 points, eight rebounds, six assists, three steals, and a block.

Lendeborg was part of a high-effort rebounding performance by the Warriors, who grabbed 44 boards to Miami's 39, even with the massive Anteotkounmpo and Bam Adebayo (18 points, 10 rebounds) manning the middle. The bench made a big difference, collecting 24 boards while the Heat's reserves got seven. Standouts were Charles Bassey, De'Anthony Melton, and Al Horford, who had seven, six, and five rebounds respectively. Bassey and Horford each scored eight points and Horford was +21, making both his threes and has five in his last two games.

Bassey played 14 "loud minutes," according to Bob Fitzgerald, and it's hard to argue with that description. He simply does a lot of stuff, even if some of that is negative (five fouls, three turnovers, airballed a three). Bassey blocked three shots and appeared to make the Heat big men decidedly uncomfortable. His most impressive play came when he grabbed a free throw rebound while getting double teamed and fouled, and flipped in a shot anyway.

Once again, the Warriors started slow and fell behind by double-digits early, mainly because they started with ice-cold shooting. The young guys kept the team afloat as the veterans slowly loosened up, with Will Richard leading the team with 10 first-half points and Yaxel adding nine.

The Warriors bench shot 19-for-30, while their Heat counterparts were 8-for-27. Nikola Jovic's long-term deal already looks regrettable. Bobby Portis tried to fire up his team by going after Georges "The Minivan" Niang, and after Niang didn't back down, Portis didn't score for the rest of the game. Niang was 4-for-5 with 10 points after halftime.

Miami sacrificed a ton of their depth to land the Greek Freak, and as a result, only Pelle Larsson is truly reliable off the bench. They're leaning on guys on the downside of their careers, like Thompson and Tim Hardaway, Jr., along with guys taken off the NBA scrap heap, like center Nick Richards. And that could have been the Warriors!

It's never been clear how realistic the Warriors' reported pursuit of Antetokounmpo was at last year's deadline, and they appeared to be a non-factor in the summer's trade talks. The Milwaukee Bucks may not have seriously wanted anyone aside from Brandin Podziemski, and if they weren't going to take Jimmy Butler back, the only way Golden State could have landed Antetokounmpo was too gut their roster and fill in the gaps with, well, guys who didn't have a lot of other options.

They also wouldn't have Yaxel, who is already better than anyone on the Heat besides Bam and Giannis. The Curry Flurry was the engine behind the team's second-half surge, but the team made their game-defining 17-3 run in the quarter by playing defense best described as "really annoying" — something that the Heat used to specialize in. Richard, Melton, Podziemski, and Lendeborg all deflected passes and closed out on threes, causing a number of low-percentage shots late in the shot clock.

Big Al had an embarrassing play where Adebayo faked him out and hit a stepback jumper in the second quarter as Horford stumbled backwards. However, in the remaining 28 minutes following that play, Horford only scored one fewer point than the 83-point man.

The game could have become a true blowout were it not for Davion Mitchell going off in the final quarter, scoring 16 points on 7-for-11 shooting and proving beyond a doubt that there's no better NBA career move than leaving the Sacramento Kings.

Brandon Williams had another solid bench effort with 10 points, four assists, and two surprising blocks. He continued to get to the rim at will off the dribble, getting layups and drawing fouls. Williams' defense has been far better than advertised, and down the stretch, he iced the game by repeatedly finding his teammates for alley-oops.

Why does Williams need to seize this opportunity so badly? He's gotta pay rent in San Francisco.

Let's just say we wouldn't be shocked if Williams is really invested in NBA Cup games and the massive payouts that go to winners. If he can secure one of the six-figure playoff shares, maybe he won't have to get extra roommates from Craigslist.

The Warriors have two more games left on this extended homestand. They'll face the Orlando Magic, missing Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs, on Saturday, then the red-hot New Orleans Pelicans Monday, who will be on a back-to-back, to the Warriors' advantage. Also to the Warriors' advantage? They're the Pelicans.

Six wins in a row, with an excellent chance to stretch their winning streak to eight games before a brutal trip to the Texas Triangle next week. Imagine how good they could be if the first few minutes of the game didn't stink!
